punctuated:
者謂之禮樂，其從事於政，特號令兵刑之末爾，何怪乎治之不古若哉？然則謂之虛名，可也。漢初去古未遠，似可與有爲矣。然以叔孫通爲之臣，緜蕞野外，竊先王糟粕之餘，秦儀雜就，爲一時苟簡之制。故魯兩生以其非興禮樂之本，而却以百年後興也。蜀漢僻處一隅，若無足有爲矣。然以諸葛亮爲之相，立綱陳紀，而不爲近圖；開誠布公，而不爲小惠。故程子謂其得禮樂之意，而許以庶幾禮樂也。
漢章帝永言前王，明發興作，詔羣臣各盡所能，至以「堯作大章，一夔足矣」擬之曹褒，志則大矣。奈何依準舊典，雜取經讖，張敏已有破亂聖術之譏，而褒不足以成其志也，后夔云乎哉？唐文皇夜讀《周禮》，以爲聖作，詔羣臣屢爲會議，至以漢章拳拳有志不就語之魏徵，心則盛矣。奈何才非命世，學無素業，主道已有必愧禮樂之論，而徵不足以副其心也，周
translation_en:
…are called rites and music, while the business of government consists merely of such peripheral matters as commands, warfare, and punishments. What wonder that government falls short of antiquity? It is therefore reasonable to call these empty names. At the beginning of the Han, antiquity was not yet distant, and something worthwhile might seemingly have been accomplished. Yet with Shusun Tong as a minister, ritual rehearsals were conducted in the open countryside with ropes and markers, appropriating the mere dregs left by the former kings and mixing in Qin ceremonial to fashion a makeshift system for the moment. Thus the two scholars of Lu, judging that this was no foundation for reviving rites and music, declined, saying that their revival should come a hundred years later. Shu Han occupied a remote corner, seemingly without sufficient scope for achievement. Yet with Zhuge Liang as its Counselor-in-chief, it established guiding principles and set forth rules without pursuing short-term schemes; it acted with sincerity and impartiality without dispensing petty favors. Master Cheng therefore said that Zhuge Liang had grasped the meaning of rites and music, and acknowledged that he had come close to realizing them.
Emperor Zhang of Han reflected continually on the former kings and rose at dawn to undertake his work, commanding his ministers each to exert his abilities fully. He even compared Cao Bao to Kui, saying, “When Yao created the Dazhang music, one Kui was enough.” His ambition was indeed great. Yet Cao Bao followed old precedents and drew indiscriminately from the Classics and apocryphal prognostications. Zhang Min had already criticized this as corrupting and confusing the sages’ methods, and Cao Bao was unequal to fulfilling the emperor’s ambition. Could he really be called another Kui, the ancient music master? Emperor Wen of Tang read the Rites of Zhou at night, regarded it as a sage’s work, and repeatedly ordered his ministers to deliberate together. He even spoke to Wei Zheng of Emperor Zhang of Han’s earnest ambition and failure to realize it. His aspiration was indeed ardent. Yet Wei Zheng’s abilities were not those of an epoch-making man, and his learning lacked a foundation of sustained study. There was already a judgment that the ruler’s way must fall short in rites and music [?], and Wei Zheng was unequal to fulfilling the emperor’s aspiration. Could he be called Zhou…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
云乎哉由此觀之後世禮樂不能復古
漢之雜霸唐之雜夷卒不免於公論歐陽
子所謂不可不出於一者豈欺我哉吐辭
爲經出言爲論六經之後世未嘗無文章
也何楊龜山槩謂之無益乎盖聖人之文
章形於言語闡造化精微之蘊著之簡冊
本仁義英華之發濂溪所謂文以載道是
也後世則以見於操脩措諸踐履者謂之
道德其從事於文第聲律詞藻之工爾何
===
怪乎文之不古若哉然則謂之無益可也
夫以柳子厚當百年積累之餘大放厥辭
以追往古江左之綺麗已除光嶽之精華
既聚一時文名與韓退之相爲頡頏而韓
亦稱其雄深雅健似司馬子長崔蔡不足
多也劉禹錫所謂文章與時高下不見於
此乎揚子雲慕司馬相如之才嘗擬其賦
已而棄不復爲作太玄以準易作法言以
擬論語一時君子唯桓譚以爲絕倫而譚

云乎哉？由此觀之，後世禮樂不能復古，漢之雜霸，唐之雜夷，卒不免於公論。歐陽子所謂不可不出於一者，豈欺我哉？吐辭爲經，出言爲論，六經之後，世未嘗無文章也。何楊龜山槩謂之無益乎？盖聖人之文章，形於言語，闡造化精微之蘊；著之簡冊，本仁義英華之發。濂溪所謂文以載道是也。後世則以見於操脩、措諸踐履者謂之道德，其從事於文，第聲律詞藻之工爾。何怪乎文之不古若哉？然則謂之無益可也。
夫以柳子厚當百年積累之餘，大放厥辭，以追往古。江左之綺麗已除，光嶽之精華既聚，一時文名與韓退之相爲頡頏，而韓亦稱其雄深雅健，似司馬子長，崔蔡不足多也。劉禹錫所謂文章與時高下，不見於此乎？揚子雲慕司馬相如之才，嘗擬其賦，已而棄不復爲，作《太玄》以準《易》，作《法言》以擬《論語》。一時君子，唯桓譚以爲絕倫，而譚
translation_en:
…could he be called a Duke of Zhou? Viewed in this light, the rites and music of later ages could not recover antiquity. The Han mixed kingly government with hegemonic methods, and the Tang mixed Chinese practices with those of foreign peoples; neither ultimately escaped public judgment. Could Master Ouyang have misled us when he said that these must issue from a single source? Their utterances became classics, their words became authoritative discourses. Since the Six Classics, the world has never lacked literary compositions. Why, then, did Yang Guishan dismiss them all as useless? The sages’ writings, expressed in words, reveal the subtle mysteries of creation; committed to books, they arise from the flowering of benevolence and righteousness. This is what Lianxi meant by writing as a vehicle for the Way. In later ages, however, people called what appeared in self-cultivation and was put into practice “the Way and virtue,” while their literary endeavors amounted merely to skill in prosody and ornate diction. Why wonder that their writing fell short of antiquity? It is therefore permissible to call it useless.
Liu Zihou, coming after a hundred years of accumulated achievement, gave full scope to his expression in pursuit of antiquity. The florid style of Jiangzuo had already been swept away, and the finest energies of heaven and earth had gathered in him. His literary reputation rivaled that of Han Tuizhi in their day. Han himself praised his writing as powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous, resembling that of Sima Zichang, with Cui and Cai scarcely worth praising by comparison. Is this not an illustration of Liu Yuxi’s saying that literature rises and falls with the times? Yang Ziyun admired Sima Xiangru’s talent and once modeled his rhapsodies on his. Later, he abandoned the genre and composed no more, writing the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) on the model of the Book of Changes and Model Sayings (Fayan) in imitation of the Analects. Among the gentlemen of his time, only Huan Tan considered him peerless, and Tan…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
又稱其文義至深議論不詭于聖人遭遇
時君則必度越諸子矣龜山所謂庶幾於
道者不以是乎漢文涉八代而衰韓退之
以六經之文爲諸儒倡橫鶩別驅汪洋大
肆學者仰之以爲山斗其徒李漢稱之有
曰周情孔思卒澤於道德仁義是謂其得
周公孔子之趣也而原道之作識用遺體
朱子譏其因文見道即程子所謂作文有
得却爲倒學之意也然推尊孔子功不下
===
孟軻氏則誠有焉唐文歷五季而弊歐陽
子慕昌黎之文必欲并轡絶驅而追與之
並天下翕然尊之為師其徒蘇軾擬之以
文王既沒文不在兹之說是謂其得文王
孔子之傳也而論性之書謂性非所先朱
子譏其未免韓病即龜山所謂性分之内
全無見處之意也然作五代史功不下司
馬遷則不誣焉由此觀之後世文章終愧
于道漢之文以貫道軾之文與道俱終未

punctuated: 又稱其文義至深，議論不詭于聖人，遭遇時君，則必度越諸子矣。龜山所謂庶幾於道者，不以是乎？漢文涉八代而衰，韓退之以六經之文爲諸儒倡，橫鶩別驅，汪洋大肆，學者仰之以爲山斗。其徒李漢稱之有曰：「周情孔思，卒澤於道德仁義。」是謂其得周公孔子之趣也。而《原道》之作，識用遺體，朱子譏其因文見道，即程子所謂作文有得，却爲倒學之意也。然推尊孔子，功不下孟軻氏，則誠有焉。唐文歷五季而弊，歐陽子慕昌黎之文，必欲并轡絶驅而追與之並，天下翕然尊之為師。其徒蘇軾擬之以「文王既沒，文不在兹」之說，是謂其得文王孔子之傳也。而《論性》之書，謂性非所先，朱子譏其未免韓病，即龜山所謂性分之内全無見處之意也。然作《五代史》，功不下司馬遷，則不誣焉。由此觀之，後世文章終愧于道。漢之文以貫道，軾之文與道俱，終未
translation_en:
…also praised the profound meaning of his writings and the agreement of his arguments with the sages: were he to encounter a receptive ruler of his age, he would surely surpass the various philosophical masters. Was this not why Guishan said that he came close to the Way?

The literary tradition of the Han declined through eight dynasties. Han Tuizhi took the writings of the Six Classics as his standard and led the scholars, ranging freely on a course of his own, expansive and unrestrained. Students looked up to him as to Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper. His follower Li Han praised him, saying: “With the sentiments of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius, he ultimately steeped himself in the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness.” This meant that he had grasped the purport of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. Yet in his Inquiry into the Way, he recognized its functioning while neglecting its underlying substance. Master Zhu criticized him for apprehending the Way through literary composition. This is precisely what Master Cheng meant when he said that gaining insight through composing prose was learning in reverse order. Nevertheless, his achievement in exalting Confucius truly was no less than that of Meng Ke.

The literary tradition of the Tang deteriorated through the Five Dynasties. Master Ouyang admired the writings of Changli and was determined to race ahead alongside him [?], catching up and drawing abreast. All under Heaven unanimously honored him as their teacher. His follower Su Shi likened him to Confucius by invoking the words, “With King Wen dead, does not this cultural tradition reside here?” This meant that he had received the tradition transmitted by King Wen and Confucius. Yet his writing On Human Nature maintained that human nature was not the first concern. Master Zhu criticized him for failing to escape Han’s failing. This is precisely what Guishan meant when he said that Ouyang had no insight whatsoever into what lies within one’s inherent nature. Nevertheless, it is no exaggeration to say that his achievement in composing the History of the Five Dynasties was no less than Sima Qian’s.

Viewed in this light, the literary writings of later ages ultimately fall short of the Way. Li Han’s conception of writing as conveying the Way, and Su Shi’s conception of writing as existing together with the Way, ultimately have not…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
合於君子朱子所謂尤不可使出於二者
真有見哉抑嘗因是而求諸孔門其荅顏
淵之問爲邦則以四代禮樂是禮樂即所
以爲治之道也其以游夏列於文學之科
是文章不在言語之末也後世失其實而
得其名舎其本而圖其末乃曰是可以爲
治爲文矣何其不思之甚也周子曰不復
古禮不變今樂而欲至治者遠矣又曰不
務道德而第以文辭爲能者藝而已有志
===
於治與文者尚其察諸
第三問
同考試官訓導陳 批 此卷五策皆可錄錄
其名實一策用占其他日務實為
國家用以追配古人子尚勉之哉
同考試官訓導于 批 美名出於當時而公
論定於後世觀於吾子所評亦可謂公論矣此殆非
有窮理之學者不能非但記問之洽而已健羨健羨

以為治之道也其以游夏列於文學之科

得其名舍其本而圖其末乃曰是可以為

===
第三問

論定於後世觀於吾子所評亦可謂公論矣此殆非
有窮理之學者不能非但記問之洽而已健羨健羨
punctuated:
合於君子。朱子所謂「尤不可使出於二者」，真有見哉！抑嘗因是而求諸孔門，其荅顏淵之問爲邦，則以四代禮樂，是禮樂即所以爲治之道也。其以游夏列於文學之科，是文章不在言語之末也。後世失其實而得其名，舎其本而圖其末，乃曰：「是可以爲治爲文矣。」何其不思之甚也！周子曰：「不復古禮，不變今樂，而欲至治者，遠矣！」又曰：「不務道德，而第以文辭爲能者，藝而已。」有志於治與文者，尚其察諸！

第三問

同考試官訓導陳批：此卷五策皆可錄，錄其名實一策，用占其他日務實，為國家用，以追配古人。子尚勉之哉！

同考試官訓導于批：美名出於當時，而公論定於後世。觀於吾子所評，亦可謂公論矣。此殆非有窮理之學者不能，非但記問之洽而已。健羨，健羨！
translation_en:
…accord with the gentleman. Master Zhu’s statement that “above all, they must not be allowed to issue from two separate sources” [?] shows true insight! Reflecting on this, I have sought further understanding in the teachings of Confucius. When he answered Yan Yuan’s question about governing a state, he prescribed the rites and music of the four dynasties. These rites and music are precisely the Way by which government is conducted. His placing You and Xia in the category of literary learning shows that literary accomplishment does not lie in the superficial refinements of speech. Later generations have lost the substance while acquiring the name, abandoning the root while pursuing the branches, yet declare: “This will suffice for governing and for writing.” How utterly thoughtless they are! Master Zhou said: “To seek perfect government without restoring ancient rites or changing the music of the present is to remain far from it!” He also said: “Those who do not devote themselves to the Way and virtue, but regard skill in literary expression alone as ability, possess merely an art.” May those who aspire to accomplishment in government and writing examine this carefully!

Third Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: All five policy essays in this script merit inclusion. We have selected the essay on name and substance, taking it as a sign that in the future he will devote himself to substantive achievement, serve the state, and come to rival the ancients. You should strive diligently!

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: A fine reputation arises in a person’s own time, but impartial judgment is settled by later generations. Looking at your assessments, I would say that they too constitute impartial judgment. Such work could hardly be accomplished without learning devoted to investigating principle; it is more than merely extensive knowledge acquired through memorization and inquiry. I admire it greatly—greatly indeed!

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官左中允劉批人物一策正欲觀士子博
極之功與品題之鑒語而能詳擇而能精此作有焉本
房之冠舍子其誰
考試官侍講學士吳批古人散見簡冊一時撮取
為對頗難下筆此子能備舉之且品評甚當其亦真有
所見者乎
古之君子惟能全天下之美行而後能享
天下之美名蓋美行存乎我有不易成美
名存乎人有不易得苟行成於我而名輒
隨之固未有不可得者然或許子之過又
豈能免後世之公議哉嗟夫麟之為麟也
以德不以形驥之為驥也以德不以力夫
物且然而况美名在人有不本諸德行者
乎然非君子有心求是名也而實大聲宏
則有不可得而辭者尚何置疑於其間哉
敢因明問所及復之襄子計成智伯之讐
深矣豫讓匕首之挾盖不能一日忘者卒
擊其衣而智伯之讐以報故曰真義士也

考試官侍講學士吳批：古人散見簡冊，一時撮取為對，頗難下筆。此子能備舉之，且品評甚當，其亦真有所見者乎！

古之君子，惟能全天下之美行，而後能享天下之美名。蓋美行存乎我，有不易成；美名存乎人，有不易得。苟行成於我，而名輒隨之，固未有不可得者。然或許子之過，又豈能免後世之公議哉！嗟夫！麟之為麟也，以德不以形；驥之為驥也，以德不以力。夫物且然，而况美名在人，有不本諸德行者乎？然非君子有心求是名也，而實大聲宏，則有不可得而辭者，尚何置疑於其間哉！敢因明問所及復之：襄子計成，智伯之讐深矣。豫讓匕首之挾，盖不能一日忘者。卒擊其衣，而智伯之讐以報，故曰：「真義士也。」
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent: This policy question on historical figures was intended precisely to assess candidates’ breadth and depth of learning and their discernment in judging people. This composition offers detailed discussion and discriminating selection. Who but you could rank first in this examining room?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting: Accounts of the ancients are scattered throughout the written records. To gather them together on the spot for an answer makes writing quite difficult. This candidate cites them comprehensively, and his assessments are most apt. Surely he possesses genuine insight!

Only by fully realizing the admirable conduct of the world could the gentlemen of antiquity enjoy the world’s fine reputations. Admirable conduct depends on oneself and is not easily achieved; a fine reputation depends on others and is not easily obtained. If one’s conduct is perfected and reputation follows accordingly, there is certainly nothing unattainable about it. Yet if praise should prove excessive [?], how could one escape the impartial judgment of later generations? Ah! What makes a qilin a qilin is its virtue, not its form; what makes a thoroughbred a thoroughbred is its virtue, not its strength. If this is true even of creatures, how could a person’s fine reputation fail to be grounded in virtuous conduct? Yet a gentleman does not deliberately seek such a reputation. When his substance is great and his renown resounding, there are honors he cannot decline. What room remains for doubt?

I venture to respond concerning the matters raised in your illuminating question. When Xiangzi’s plot succeeded, the wrong to be avenged for Zhi Bo was profound. Yu Rang carried a dagger, for he could not forget that wrong for even a day. Finally, he struck Xiangzi’s robe, and thereby avenged Zhi Bo. Thus he was called “a truly righteous man.”

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
使襄子知而全之不爲人臣之勸乎匈奴
報至文帝之慮切矣周亞夫細柳之屯盖
方爲時所仗者竟行其令而天子之詔不
聞故曰真将軍也使文帝從而忌之是豈
任将之道乎魏相輔宣帝於中興之日而
其諫伐西域爲識兵畧作明堂月令議爲
達時令王通稱爲真漢相者非但以其能
稱上意而已賈逵當豫州凋弊之秋而外
糾貪殘以正憲度內脩政事以安吏民曹
===
丕稱爲真刺史者則以其能舉職任云爾
武德之議廢立而舉朝中立者誰不利怵
而威懼乎蕭瑀獨守正以定國儲真社稷
臣之稱太宗非以其有定守歟李密之欲
歸降而将佐貪功者誰不表獻其土地乎
李勣獨留俟密之自獻真純臣之稱太宗
非以其無所利歟書曰儆戒無虞而太平
可樂則李吉甫之面諛也李絳廷斥不避
最得大臣之體憲宗稱爲真宰相者盖見

punctuated: 使襄子知而全之，不爲人臣之勸乎？匈奴報至，文帝之慮切矣。周亞夫細柳之屯，盖方爲時所仗者，竟行其令，而天子之詔不聞，故曰真将軍也。使文帝從而忌之，是豈任将之道乎？魏相輔宣帝於中興之日，而其諫伐西域，爲識兵畧；作《明堂月令議》，爲達時令。王通稱爲真漢相者，非但以其能稱上意而已。賈逵當豫州凋弊之秋，而外糾貪殘以正憲度，內脩政事以安吏民。曹丕稱爲真刺史者，則以其能舉職任云爾。武德之議廢立，而舉朝中立者，誰不利怵而威懼乎？蕭瑀獨守正以定國儲，真社稷臣之稱，太宗非以其有定守歟？李密之欲歸降，而将佐貪功者，誰不表獻其土地乎？李勣獨留俟密之自獻，真純臣之稱，太宗非以其無所利歟？《書》曰：「儆戒無虞。」而太平可樂，則李吉甫之面諛也。李絳廷斥不避，最得大臣之體。憲宗稱爲真宰相者，盖見
translation_en:
…Had Xiangzi understood this and spared him, would that not have encouraged those who serve as subjects? When reports of the Xiongnu arrived, Emperor Wen’s concern was acute. Zhou Yafu’s encampment at Xiliu was precisely what the situation required as a bulwark. His own orders were enforced throughout, while the Son of Heaven’s edict went unheeded; hence he was called a true general. Had Emperor Wen thereupon become suspicious of him, could this have been the proper way to employ a general?

Wei Xiang assisted Emperor Xuan during the restoration of Han fortunes. His remonstrance against attacking the Western Regions showed his understanding of military strategy; his Discussion of the Bright Hall and the Monthly Ordinances showed his understanding of seasonal regulations. Wang Tong called him a true Han chief minister, and not merely because he could satisfy the sovereign’s wishes. Jia Kui served when Yuzhou was impoverished and in decline. Externally, he disciplined the corrupt and cruel to rectify the enforcement of laws; internally, he improved administration to bring peace to officials and people. Cao Pi called him a true regional inspector simply because he fulfilled the responsibilities of his office.

When the question of deposing and installing an heir was debated during the Wude reign, who among those at court who remained neutral was not tempted by advantage and frightened by power? Xiao Yu alone upheld what was right and secured the position of the heir apparent. Was it not because of his steadfast principles that Emperor Taizong called him a true minister of the altars of soil and grain? When Li Mi wished to surrender and submit, who among the commanders and their assistants who coveted credit did not propose to present his territory to the throne? Li Ji alone held back, waiting for Li Mi to offer it himself. Was it not because he sought no personal advantage that Emperor Taizong called him a truly pure minister?

The Book of Documents says: “Be vigilant and wary when there is no cause for anxiety.” Yet Li Jifu flattered the emperor to his face by saying that peace was something to enjoy. Li Jiang denounced him at court without shrinking back, displaying to the highest degree the proper bearing of a great minister. Emperor Xianzong called him a true chief minister, for he was recognized …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
知於其君如此語曰不辱君命而遣使雲
中則宋室之屈辱也洪皓氣不少挫卒全
使臣之節金人稱為真忠臣者盖見重於
外夷如此李沆相真宗嘗以四方水旱預
警其心厥後泰侈並興所言竟驗王旦嘆
其先識而稱之為真聖人然亦晚矣唐介
劾文彥博謂以間金竒錦進由妃嬪四方
聞其直言而稱之為真御史貶亦榮矣學
士代王言草詔其職也而宋實則當建儲
===
者王珪面受仁宗之命然後操筆歐陽脩
以真學士稱之則嘉其得慎重之意故爾
侍講備經筵進講其職也而邇英則當坐
講者程頤講說哲宗之前聳動羣聽文彥
博以真侍講稱之則重其得進講之體故
爾唐時有司鮮不市恩覬意挺立頹波中
乃有王丘崔沔裴耀卿者一則餼牽外無
他獻一則供帳無錦繡一則表獻數百言
以寓規諫玄宗總以真良吏稱之三人而

translation_en: …such was the recognition he received from his ruler. The saying goes: “Do not dishonor your ruler’s commission.” Yet sending an envoy to Yunzhong was a humiliation for the Song ruling house. Hong Hao’s spirit did not falter in the slightest, and he ultimately preserved his integrity as an envoy. The Jin people called him a truly loyal minister: such was the esteem he commanded among foreign peoples. When Li Hang served as chief councilor to Zhenzong, he repeatedly alerted the emperor to floods and droughts throughout the realm, forewarning him. Later, extravagance and luxury arose together, and his words proved true. Wang Dan marveled at his foresight and called him a true sage, but by then it was too late. Tang Jie impeached Wen Yanbo, saying that he had presented extraordinary gold-woven brocades through the imperial consorts. People everywhere heard of his forthright words and called him a true censor; even his demotion brought him honor. An Academician speaks on the sovereign’s behalf, and drafting edicts is his duty. In the Song, when an heir apparent was to be established [?], Wang Gui personally received Renzong’s command before taking up his brush. Ouyang Xiu called him a true Academician because he commended his understanding of the need for caution and gravity. An Expositor attends the Classics Colloquium, and delivering lectures is his duty. At the Yingying Hall, where lectures were delivered seated, Cheng Yi lectured before Zhezong and stirred all who listened. Wen Yanbo called him a true Expositor because he valued his grasp of the proper manner of lecturing. In Tang times, few officials refrained from courting favor and anticipating the ruler’s wishes. Yet Wang Qiu, Cui Mian, and Pei Yaoqing stood firm amid this tide of decline. One presented nothing beyond provisions and livestock; another supplied furnishings without embroidered silks; and the third presented a memorial of several hundred words that conveyed admonition and remonstrance. Xuanzong called them all truly good officials—three men, and …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不以為罪此蓋其初政清明乎過此則其
志荒矣蒙古諸臣鮮有全材孰意超出風
氣外乃有廉希憲者居相臣位以勳業著
聞受孔子戒以忠孝自負當時兼以宰相
中真宰相男子中真男子稱之一人而不
以為嫌此蓋其善變國俗乎下此則可稱
者少矣噫天下美名其實難副而真之為
言又皆確然之詞鸞停鵠峙播揚人口珠
聯璧合照映簡編千載之下使人聞之寧
===
不為諸君子歆艷也耶抑尤有說焉程頤
一代真儒道尊河洛李沆一時賢相名冠
元臣唐介之直同於李絳洪皓之節幾於
豫讓之數公者吾無間然乃若魏相功業
著矣而嚴切是尚有乖相體於當時王珪
文學著矣而三旨是名頗尸相位於他日
蕭瑀早失河池之節不得與堯君素而齊
名李勣贊成武氏之立乃甘與許敬宗而
同惡其顯著者且如此他可知矣然則眾

不爲諸君子歆豔也耶抑尤有説焉程顥
一代眞儒道尊河洛李沆一時賢相名冠
元臣唐介之直同於李絳洪皓之節幾於
蘇武謙讓之數公者吾無間然乃若貌相
著矣而嚴切是尚有乖相體於當時王珪
文學著矣而三旨是名類尸相位於他日
蕭鶚未失河池之節不得與兗君壽和齊
名李勣積歲武氏之立乃甘與許敬宗而
同惡其顯著者且如此他可知矣然則衆
punctuated:
不以為罪，此蓋其初政清明乎？過此則其志荒矣。蒙古諸臣鮮有全材，孰意超出風氣外，乃有廉希憲者，居相臣位，以勳業著聞；受孔子戒，以忠孝自負。當時兼以「宰相中真宰相，男子中真男子」稱之一人，而不以為嫌，此蓋其善變國俗乎？下此則可稱者少矣。噫！天下美名，其實難副，而「真」之為言，又皆確然之詞。鸞停鵠峙，播揚人口；珠聯璧合，照映簡編。千載之下，使人聞之，寧不為諸君子歆艷也耶？
抑尤有說焉。程頤，一代真儒，道尊河洛；李沆，一時賢相，名冠元臣。唐介之直，同於李絳；洪皓之節，幾於豫讓。之數公者，吾無間然。乃若魏相，功業著矣，而嚴切是尚，有乖相體於當時；王珪，文學著矣，而三旨是名，頗尸相位於他日。蕭瑀早失河池之節，不得與堯君素而齊名；李勣贊成武氏之立，乃甘與許敬宗而同惡。其顯著者且如此，他可知矣。然則眾
translation_en:
… and did not regard it as an offense. Was this perhaps because his government in its early years was clear and enlightened? Thereafter, his aspirations went astray. Among the ministers of the Mongols, few possessed comprehensive talent. Who would have expected someone to rise above the prevailing customs as Lian Xixian did? Occupying the position of chief minister, he became renowned for his meritorious achievements; accepting the precepts of Confucius, he prided himself on loyalty and filial devotion. At the time, people applied both descriptions to this one man: “a true chief minister among chief ministers” and “a true man among men,” without finding this objectionable. Was this perhaps because he excelled at transforming his people’s customs? Below his standard, few deserved praise. Alas! Fine reputations in this world are difficult to live up to, and the word “true” is, moreover, an unequivocal assertion. Like luan birds at rest and swans standing tall, these men’s praises circulated on everyone’s lips; like strung pearls and paired jade discs, they illuminated the written records. A thousand years later, could anyone hearing of them fail to admire and envy these gentlemen?
Yet there is more to be said. Cheng Yi was a true Confucian of his age, whose Way was revered in the He–Luo region; Li Hang was a worthy chief minister of his time, whose reputation stood foremost among the senior ministers. Tang Jie’s uprightness equaled Li Jiang’s, and Hong Hao’s integrity approached Yu Rang’s. With these several gentlemen [?], I can find no fault. As for Wei Xiang, his achievements were illustrious, but his preference for severity and exacting demands departed from the proper bearing of a chief minister in his day. Wang Gui was renowned for literary learning, but he earned the name “Three Directives” and, in his later years, largely occupied the chief minister’s position without fulfilling its duties. Xiao Yu early forfeited his integrity at Hechi and could not rank alongside Yao Junsu in reputation. Li Ji supported the installation of Lady Wu and willingly shared in Xu Jingzong’s wrongdoing. If even the conspicuous examples were like this, the others can readily be imagined. If so, the multitude …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
人所稱者豈皆確論哉雖然擇從其善聖
人之訓取法乎上君子之心就其中可以
為終身師範者則伊川其尤也鄙見如斯
未知能協天下公議否執事幸進教之
第四問
陳沛
同考試官學正周批
天資學術皆可以建
立事功學術之偏適足以誤人家國此策於漢宋諸
人歷歷言之固見所學於末又斷以天資學術不可
===
偏廢深為有見錄之不能無補
考試官左中允劉批
天資之美固當養以學術
而學術尤貴於正古人事業未有不以是為重輕者此
策歷能評之末復歸重於學有識之士也高薦允宜
考試官侍講學士吳批
古人事業奇偉皆從學術
中流出間有可議者則以學術不正故耳子於是問能
以是意答之卓有定見可嘉可嘉
古人之事業有出於天資者焉有發自學
術者焉養之純者其為也有本而自無不

考試官左中允劉　批〔天資之美固當養以學術而學術尤貴於正古人事業未有不以是爲重輕者此策歷能評之末復歸重於學有識之士也高薦允宜〕

古人之事業有出於天資者焉有發自學
術者焉養之純者其爲也有本而自無不
punctuated:
人所稱者，豈皆確論哉？雖然，擇從其善，聖人之訓；取法乎上，君子之心。就其中可以為終身師範者，則伊川其尤也。鄙見如斯，未知能協天下公議否？執事幸進教之。
第四問
陳沛
同考試官學正周批：天資、學術皆可以建立事功。學術之偏，適足以誤人家國。此策於漢宋諸人歷歷言之，固見所學；於末又斷以天資、學術不可偏廢，深為有見，錄之不能無補。
考試官左中允劉批：天資之美，固當養以學術，而學術尤貴於正。古人事業，未有不以是為重輕者。此策歷能評之，末復歸重於學，有識之士也，高薦允宜。
考試官侍講學士吳批：古人事業奇偉，皆從學術中流出。間有可議者，則以學術不正故耳。子於是問，能以是意答之，卓有定見，可嘉可嘉。
古人之事業，有出於天資者焉，有發自學術者焉。養之純者，其為也有本，而自無不
translation_en:
…are the judgments concerning those whom people praise all sound? Nevertheless, choosing what is good in others and following it is the sage’s teaching; taking the highest as one’s model is the gentleman’s aspiration. Among these men who might serve as lifelong teachers and models, Yichuan is preeminent. Such is my humble view; I do not know whether it accords with the impartial judgment of all under Heaven. May you kindly instruct me.
Fourth Question
Chen Pei
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: Both natural endowment and learning can provide the means to establish achievements. Bias in learning, however, serves only to lead people astray, to the detriment of their families and the state. This policy essay discusses the various men of the Han and Song individually and clearly, demonstrating the writer’s learning. At its close, it further concludes that neither natural endowment nor learning may be neglected. This shows considerable insight; selecting it for inclusion cannot fail to be beneficial.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Secretariat Rectifier: Excellence of natural endowment certainly ought to be nurtured through learning, and in learning, correctness is especially prized. The achievements of the ancients invariably gained or lost in worth on this account. This policy essay assesses them one by one and, at its close, once again places the chief emphasis on learning. Its author is a man of discernment; recommending him highly is entirely fitting.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Waiting: The extraordinary and magnificent achievements of the ancients all flowed from their learning. Where there were occasional grounds for criticism, these arose simply because their learning was not correct. In answering this question, you have been able to respond with this understanding, showing outstanding clarity and firmness of judgment. Admirable indeed!
Among the achievements of the ancients, some arose from natural endowment, while others sprang from learning. Those whose cultivation was pure had a foundation for their actions, and naturally there was nothing that did not…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
盛禀之厚者亦往往暗合而不無可觀故
天資近道或有非學術所能先而學術有
未正焉又不若天資暗合者之爲愈也君
子之於人物豈可以一律評哉請以所聞
復執事之問漢高帝之臣有周勃者焉起
于織薄而封絳侯爲人重厚少文坐責諸
生趣爲我語其木強可知也而帝獨以可
屬大事安劉必勃許之於是左袒一呼誅
呂立代竟成社稷之功史稱其爲漢伊周
===
非許之哉古所謂木訥近仁者盖以此也
武帝之臣有霍光者焉階自去病而封博
陸爲人不學無術洪範未聞桐宫罔識其

負成王賜之於是委裘有托擁昭立宣再
定廟堂之策史稱其雖伊周不過非美之
哉古所稱篤實不揜者盖以此也契丹入
寇羽書五至其勢盖岌岌矣主親征之議
畫百年之策而飲酒放歌笑謔自如卒之

非許之哉古所謂木訥近仁者蓋以此也

陸爲人不學無術洪範未聞桐宮罔識其
膚陋可知也而帝獨以可任大事圖周公
負成王賜之於是委裘有托擁昭立宣再
定廟堂之策史稱其雖伊周不過非美之
哉古所稱篤以不揜者蓋以此也契丹入
寇羽書五至其勢蓋岌岌矣主親征之議
畫百年之策而飲酒放歌笑謔自如卒之
punctuated:
盛。禀之厚者，亦往往暗合而不無可觀。故天資近道，或有非學術所能先；而學術有未正焉，又不若天資暗合者之爲愈也。君子之於人物，豈可以一律評哉？請以所聞復執事之問。
漢高帝之臣有周勃者焉，起于織薄而封絳侯。爲人重厚少文，坐責諸生：「趣爲我語！」其木強可知也。而帝獨以可屬大事、安劉必勃許之。於是左袒一呼，誅呂立代，竟成社稷之功。史稱其爲漢伊周，非許之哉？古所謂木訥近仁者，盖以此也。
武帝之臣有霍光者焉，階自去病而封博陸。爲人不學無術，《洪範》未聞，桐宫罔識，其膚陋可知也。而帝獨以可任大事，圖周公負成王賜之。於是委裘有托，擁昭立宣，再定廟堂之策。史稱其雖伊周不過，非美之哉？古所稱篤實不揜者，盖以此也。
契丹入寇，羽書五至，其勢盖岌岌矣。主親征之議，畫百年之策，而飲酒放歌，笑謔自如，卒之
translation_en:
…flourish. Those richly endowed by nature also often accord with the Way without consciously seeking it, and their achievements are by no means unworthy of regard. Thus, when natural gifts approach the Way, they may accomplish things that scholarly learning cannot surpass. When learning is not correct, it is inferior to a natural endowment that accords with the Way unawares. How could a gentleman judge all men by a single standard? Allow me to answer your question with what I have learned.
Among the ministers of Emperor Gao of Han was Zhou Bo, who rose from weaving screens [?] to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang. He was grave and substantial in character but possessed little literary cultivation. Remaining seated, he would rebuke the scholars: “Hurry up and tell me!” His blunt obstinacy is evident from this. Yet the emperor singled him out as someone who could be entrusted with great affairs, declaring that it would surely be Bo who secured the Liu house. Thereupon, with a single call for men to bare their left arms, he destroyed the Lü clan and enthroned the ruler of Dai, ultimately rendering great service to the dynasty. The histories call him the Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou of the Han: is this not praise? This surely exemplifies the ancient saying that the plain and slow of speech are close to benevolence.
Among the ministers of Emperor Wu was Huo Guang, who advanced through his connection with Huo Qubing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu. He lacked learning and scholarly method: he had never heard of the “Great Plan” and knew nothing of the Tong Palace. His superficial knowledge and ignorance are evident from this. Yet the emperor singled him out as someone capable of bearing responsibility for great affairs and bestowed upon him a painting of the Duke of Zhou carrying King Cheng on his back. Thus the imperial succession had someone to whom it could be entrusted: he supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan, twice settling the court’s great questions. The histories say that even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou did not surpass him: is this not commendation? This surely exemplifies what the ancients praised as substantial integrity that cannot be obscured.
When the Khitan invaded and urgent military dispatches arrived five times, the situation was indeed precarious. He advocated that the emperor lead the campaign in person and devised a plan for a hundred years of security, yet drank wine and sang freely, laughing and joking as usual. In the end…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
點虜請盟弭兵南北寇萊公之績何偉也
張詠謂其不學無術比之霍光盖責備賢
者之意愚則曰天資英邁通春秋三傳豈
真光之流乎兩宫搆隙中外危懼其時盖
洶洶矣勸其母以慈勉其子以孝而垂紳
正笏不動聲色卒之光獻撤簾嗣君秉政
韓魏公之功何竒也吕中謂其重厚可任
比之周勃盖即其近似者為名愚則曰獨
觀書文晝夜不寐豈真勃之匹乎程子於
===
子房謂其有儒者氣象非以其功成引退
不邇榮利故邪然運籌帷幄之中决勝千
里之外要之不無所自學禮淮陽受書圯
上其學固有素矣程子於陳平謂其不知
道而知學非以其善言宰職為得大體故
邪然出竒裨開拓之業交歡成定策之功
要之必有所本家貧讀書治黃老術其學
亦已舊矣若漢武帝下詔求賢臨軒策問
而公孫弘起跡羊豕立談封侯正宜開陳

不𢿘榮利故邪然運籌帷幄之中决勝千
里之外要之不無所自學禮淮陽受書圯

道而知學非以其善言宰職爲得大體故
邪然出奇裨開拓之業交歡成定策之功
要之必有所本家貧讀書治黄老術其學
亦已舊矣若漢武帝下詔求賢臨軒策問
而公孫弘起跡羊豕立談封侯正宜開陳
punctuated:
點虜請盟，弭兵南北，寇萊公之績何偉也！張詠謂其不學無術，比之霍光，盖責備賢者之意。愚則曰：天資英邁，通春秋三傳，豈真光之流乎？兩宫搆隙，中外危懼，其時盖洶洶矣。勸其母以慈，勉其子以孝，而垂紳正笏，不動聲色，卒之光獻撤簾，嗣君秉政，韓魏公之功何竒也！吕中謂其重厚可任，比之周勃，盖即其近似者為名。愚則曰：獨觀書文，晝夜不寐，豈真勃之匹乎？

程子於子房，謂其有儒者氣象，非以其功成引退，不邇榮利故邪？然運籌帷幄之中，决勝千里之外，要之不無所自。學禮淮陽，受書圯上，其學固有素矣。程子於陳平，謂其不知道而知學，非以其善言宰職，為得大體故邪？然出竒裨開拓之業，交歡成定策之功，要之必有所本。家貧讀書，治黃老術，其學亦已舊矣。

若漢武帝下詔求賢，臨軒策問，而公孫弘起跡羊豕，立談封侯，正宜開陳
translation_en:
…the enemy sought a covenant [?], and warfare ceased between north and south. How great were the achievements of Kou, Duke of Lai! Zhang Yong called him unlearned and lacking in skill, comparing him to Huo Guang; his intention was presumably to demand perfection of a worthy man. I, in my humble opinion, would say: endowed with outstanding natural gifts and versed in the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, could he really have been of Huo Guang’s sort? When a rift developed between the two palaces, fear gripped court and country, and great turmoil prevailed. He urged the mother to show maternal kindness and encouraged the son to show filial devotion. With his ceremonial sash hanging down and his audience tablet held upright, he betrayed no agitation in voice or expression. In the end, Empress Dowager Guangxian withdrew the curtain of her regency, and the succeeding emperor assumed government. How extraordinary were the accomplishments of Han, Duke of Wei! Lü Zhong described him as grave, substantial, and fit to be entrusted with responsibility, comparing him to Zhou Bo; presumably he characterized him by their points of resemblance. I, in my humble opinion, would say: reading books and writings alone, foregoing sleep day and night, could he really have been merely Zhou Bo’s equal?

Master Cheng said that Zifang had the bearing of a Confucian scholar. Was this not because, his achievements complete, he retired and kept his distance from honors and profit? Yet his planning within the command tent and determining victory a thousand li away must, after all, have had some source. He studied ritual in Huaiyang and received a book upon a bridge: his learning certainly had longstanding foundations. Master Cheng said of Chen Ping that, though he did not understand the Way, he understood the importance of learning. Was this not because his skillful account of a chief minister’s duties grasped their essential principles? Yet his ingenious stratagems aided the work of expanding the realm, and his cultivation of friendly relations secured the achievement of settling the succession. These, after all, must have had some foundation. He read books despite his family’s poverty and studied the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi: his learning, too, was of long standing.

When Emperor Wu of Han issued an edict seeking worthy men and personally posed policy questions from his throne, Gongsun Hong rose from tending sheep and pigs and, through his speeches, was enfeoffed as a marquis. Surely he ought to have expounded…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
善道以承德意可也柰何誣水旱以文其
奸假儉約以售其詐徙仲舒於膠東陷主
父於刑戮而帝之好大喜功窮兵黷武曾
不能少救則其習春秋爲業以文學見徵
者豈非希世取寵之筌蹄乎趙普以潜邸
受知事無大小悉以咨决而獻可替否偃
武脩文有以定一代之規盖其少習吏事
素寡學術晚年讀書手不釋卷而遇斷大
議取决方冊所得於論語者爲獨深也不
===
然則其自稱載披典籍頗識前言者果何
物耶李沆以科甲被遇事關軍國必訪裁
處而四方水旱日以奏聞中外利害一切
報罷有以得大臣之體盖沆少而好學器
識宏遠詔書應制文理稱旨而節用愛人
使民以時體驗於論語者爲尤切也不然
則其同列稱爲聖人當時號曰聖相者果
何謂邪若宋神宗銳意太平諏諮治道而
王安石歡同魚水驟遷端揆正當日進讜

何謂邪若宋神宗銳意太平詠諮治道而
王安石歡同魚水驟遷端揆正當日進儆
punctuated: 善道，以承德意，可也。柰何誣水旱以文其奸，假儉約以售其詐，徙仲舒於膠東，陷主父於刑戮，而帝之好大喜功、窮兵黷武，曾不能少救？則其習《春秋》爲業、以文學見徵者，豈非希世取寵之筌蹄乎？趙普以潜邸受知，事無大小，悉以咨决，而獻可替否，偃武脩文，有以定一代之規。盖其少習吏事，素寡學術，晚年讀書，手不釋卷，而遇斷大議，取决方冊，所得於《論語》者爲獨深也。不然，則其自稱「載披典籍，頗識前言」者，果何物耶？李沆以科甲被遇，事關軍國，必訪裁處，而四方水旱，日以奏聞，中外利害，一切報罷，有以得大臣之體。盖沆少而好學，器識宏遠，詔書應制，文理稱旨，而「節用愛人，使民以時」，體驗於《論語》者爲尤切也。不然，則其同列稱爲聖人，當時號曰聖相者，果何謂邪？若宋神宗銳意太平，諏諮治道，而王安石歡同魚水，驟遷端揆，正當日進讜
translation_en:
…sound principles, thereby responding to the emperor’s benevolent intentions: this would have been proper. Why, instead, did he misrepresent floods and droughts to cloak his wickedness, and feign frugality to put his deceit into effect, transfer Dong Zhongshu to Jiaodong, and bring Zhufu Yan to execution, while doing nothing whatsoever to curb the emperor’s appetite for grand achievements and military adventurism? Was not his pursuit of the Spring and Autumn Annals as a specialty, and his summons to office for literary learning, merely a means of pandering to the age and winning favor?

Zhao Pu won the emperor’s confidence before his accession. In matters great and small, the emperor consulted him for decisions. By recommending what was right and correcting what was wrong, laying aside arms and cultivating civil government, he helped establish the guiding rules of a dynasty. In his youth he had learned administrative business but had little scholarly learning. In his later years he read constantly, never putting down his books; when deciding major questions, he sought guidance in written texts. His understanding of the Analects was particularly profound. Otherwise, what could he have meant when he said of himself, “I have repeatedly perused the canonical writings and have some knowledge of the sayings of the ancients”?

Li Hang gained imperial favor through success in the examinations. Whenever affairs concerned the military or the state, the emperor invariably consulted him about their disposition. He reported daily on floods and droughts throughout the realm, while proposals concerning benefits and harms at court and in the provinces were all rejected. In this he exemplified the proper bearing of a great minister. From his youth, Hang loved learning and possessed broad capacity and far-reaching discernment. His edicts and compositions written at imperial command pleased the emperor in their language and reasoning. In particular, he put into practice the Analects’ teaching to “be frugal in expenditure and cherish the people; employ the people at the proper seasons.” Otherwise, why did his colleagues call him a sage, and his contemporaries style him the “sage chief councilor”?

When Emperor Shenzong of the Song set his heart on achieving peace and good government and sought counsel on the way to govern, Wang Anshi enjoyed a rapport with him like that between fish and water and rose swiftly to become chief councilor. He ought then to have offered forthright counsel daily…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
猷以答殊遇可也奈何變舊章而作新法
斥忠直而進小人始以萬言之書終以三
不足之說使羣姦得志毒流四海人皆爲
諱言則其以文章節行爲高以道德經濟
爲任者豈非欺世盜名之捷徑乎抑嘗因
是而爲之說資稟得之天學力養之人二
者可兼有而不可偏廢也有天資而不輔
之以學雖其建立事功倉卒有濟而規模
疎略無以爲經遠之圖有學術而不本之
===
以正雖其志節衒露若可有爲而聲聞過
情不可責以實用此絳侯博陸不免身家
之及而平津荊國之誤人家國不淺也孔
子以天縱之聖猶好古敏以求之顏淵以
生知之亞至於欲罷不能然則天資之美
者豈可恃而不學其爲學者又可不以孔
顏爲法邪
第五問
劉楷

===

情不可責以實用此絳侯博陸不免身家
之及而平津荊國之誤人家國不淺也孔
子以天縱之聖猶好古敏以求之顔淵以
生知之亞至於欲罷不能然則天資之美
者豈可恃而不學其爲學者又可不以孔
顔爲法邪
第五問
punctuated:
猷，以答殊遇可也。奈何變舊章而作新法，斥忠直而進小人，始以萬言之書，終以三不足之說，使羣姦得志，毒流四海，人皆爲諱言，則其以文章節行爲高，以道德經濟爲任者，豈非欺世盜名之捷徑乎？抑嘗因是而爲之說：資稟得之天，學力養之人，二者可兼有而不可偏廢也。有天資而不輔之以學，雖其建立事功，倉卒有濟，而規模疎略，無以爲經遠之圖；有學術而不本之以正，雖其志節衒露，若可有爲，而聲聞過情，不可責以實用。此絳侯、博陸不免身家之及，而平津、荊國之誤人家國不淺也。孔子以天縱之聖，猶好古，敏以求之；顏淵以生知之亞，至於欲罷不能。然則天資之美者，豈可恃而不學？其爲學者，又可不以孔顏爲法邪？

第五問
劉楷
translation_en:
…counsels, thereby repaying the exceptional favor he had received. Why, then, did he alter established institutions and introduce the New Policies, dismiss the loyal and upright and advance petty men? Beginning with his memorial of ten thousand words and ending with his doctrine of the “three things not to be heeded,” he allowed a host of evil men to realize their ambitions and their poison to spread throughout the realm, until everyone avoided speaking of it. Were his claims to distinction in literary accomplishment and moral integrity, and his professed commitment to morality and statecraft, then anything but a shortcut to deceiving the world and stealing a reputation?

I have therefore ventured to offer this explanation: natural endowments come from Heaven, while the strength acquired through learning is cultivated by human effort. The two can be possessed together, and neither should be neglected. Someone with natural gifts who does not supplement them with learning may accomplish deeds of service and meet sudden emergencies, yet his plans will be sketchy and inadequate as a basis for governing with a view to the distant future. Someone with learning who does not root it in rectitude may make an impressive display of resolve and integrity and seem capable of achievement, yet his reputation exceeds the reality, and he cannot be counted on for practical service. This is why the Marquis of Jiang, Zhou Bo, and the Marquis of Bolu, Huo Guang, could not prevent calamity from reaching themselves or their families, while the Marquis of Pingjin, Gongsun Hong, and the Duke of Jing, Wang Anshi, did no small harm to others’ households and states.

Confucius, though a sage endowed by Heaven, still loved antiquity and diligently sought its learning. Yan Yuan, who ranked just below those born with knowledge, reached the point where he could not stop even if he wished. How, then, can those with fine natural gifts rely on them and neglect learning? And how can those who pursue learning fail to take Confucius and Yan Yuan as their models?

Fifth Question
Liu Kai

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正鄭批時務策正欲觀士子
用世之學此卷於西山先生所謂四事十害者條析
無遺末復說出時弊頗切經生知此殆有用之學也
他日效用慎毋忘斯言
考試官左中允劉批四事十害發自長沙西山
經濟之學見諸行事者也是篇條答無遺又有發西山
所未發者蓋嘗以經濟究心也佳士佳士
考試官侍講學士吳批政經數語有關治道非細
此文忠公所望於天下後世者惜少能舉行之耳是策
能歷道之識之高才之贍而痛恤民隱之意溢於言表
===
其殆諳練世故而有槩於中者乎
嘗謂司民社者必先有愛民之心而後有
惠民之政蓋心主乎中則惠民之政無不
舉政舉於外則愛民之心有所施司民社
者果能相與如是而斯民有不受福者乎
是道也其惟古之良吏以之而今之有司
所當取法也蓋嘗聞之有司者斯民父母
斯民者有司赤子故詩有民之父母之稱

此文忠公所望於天下後世者惜少能舉行之耳是策
能歷道之識之高才之贍而痛恤民隱之意溢於言表
其殆諳練世故而有槩於中者乎
===
嘗謂司民社者必先有愛民之心而後有
惠民之政蓋心主乎中則惠民之政無不
舉政舉於外則愛民之心有所施司民社
者畀能相與如是而斯民有不受福者乎
是道也其惟古之良吏以之而今之有司
所當取法也蓋嘗聞之有司者斯民父母
斯民者有司赤子故詩有民之父母之□
punctuated:
同考試官學正鄭批：時務策，正欲觀士子用世之學。此卷於西山先生所謂四事十害者，條析無遺，末復說出時弊頗切。經生知此，殆有用之學也。他日效用，慎毋忘斯言。

考試官左中允劉批：四事十害，發自長沙西山，經濟之學見諸行事者也。是篇條答無遺，又有發西山所未發者，蓋嘗以經濟究心也。佳士！佳士！

考試官侍講學士吳批：《政經》數語，有關治道非細，此文忠公所望於天下後世者，惜少能舉行之耳。是策能歷道之，識之高，才之贍，而痛恤民隱之意溢於言表，其殆諳練世故而有槩於中者乎？

嘗謂司民社者，必先有愛民之心，而後有惠民之政。蓋心主乎中，則惠民之政無不舉；政舉於外，則愛民之心有所施。司民社者果能相與如是，而斯民有不受福者乎？是道也，其惟古之良吏以之，而今之有司所當取法也。蓋嘗聞之：有司者，斯民父母；斯民者，有司赤子。故《詩》有「民之父母」之稱。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Policy questions on current affairs are intended precisely to assess candidates’ learning for practical service in the world. This paper analyzes, item by item and without omission, what Master Xishan called the four matters and ten evils. At the end it also identifies present abuses with considerable pertinence. A student of the Classics who understands this surely possesses learning of practical use. When you enter service in the future, take care not to forget these words.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Mentor: The four matters and ten evils originated with Xishan of Changsha; they represent learning in statecraft manifested in administrative practice. This essay answers each point without omission and also develops points that Xishan himself did not develop. Clearly, the candidate has devoted serious thought to statecraft. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Examiner Wu, Academician Expositor-in-waiting: The few statements in the Classic of Governance (Zhengjing) have no small bearing on the Way of government. They express what Lord Wenzhong hoped for throughout the realm and in later generations; regrettably, few have been able to put them into practice. This policy essay can recount them all in turn. Its lofty discernment, ample talent, and profound concern for the people’s hidden sufferings overflow beyond the words themselves. Surely its author is well versed in worldly affairs and inwardly stirred by them?

I have often maintained that those responsible for the people and the altars of the soil must first possess a heart that loves the people before they can institute government that benefits them. When this heart governs within, every measure beneficial to the people will be implemented; when those measures are carried out externally, the heart that loves the people finds expression. If those responsible for the people and the altars of the soil could indeed all act in this way, could any of these people fail to receive blessings? This Way was surely followed by the good officials of antiquity, and it is what today’s officials ought to take as their model. For I have heard it said: officials are the parents of these people, and these people are the infant children of their officials. Thus the Book of Odes uses the expression “the people’s father and mother”…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
書有如保赤子之說正此謂耳夫今之人
民即昔之人民也今之土地即昔之土地
也然昔號富饒而今多窮困之家昔稱沃
壤而今多荒蕪之嘆何相去若是殊哉噫
我知其故矣蓋
朝廷設官本以為民而有司入官鮮能為
國因之以天時告災之頻加之以潢池弄兵
之慘安望地不荒蕪而民不窮困也哉然
則如之何而可無亦責之今日有司乎蓋
===
大而受一方之寄則有藩臬藩臬各有僚
屬焉小而受一郡一州一邑之寄則有守
令守令亦各有僚屬焉是皆謂之有司而
繫斯民休戚者也而可以弗加之意乎愚
嘗讀西山先生之書而得所以治民之法
矣蓋西山帥長沙時嘗勸其僚屬勉四事
而去十害今其言固在豈非後人之龜鑑
哉其所謂律己以廉也撫民以仁也存心
以公也蒞事以勤也此之謂四事豈不以

蓋大而受一方之寄，則有藩臬，藩臬各有僚屬焉；小而受一郡一州一邑之寄，則有守令，守令亦各有僚屬焉。是皆謂之有司，而繫斯民休戚者也，而可以弗加之意乎？愚嘗讀西山先生之書，而得所以治民之法矣。蓋西山帥長沙時，嘗勸其僚屬勉四事而去十害。今其言固在，豈非後人之龜鑑哉？其所謂律己以廉也，撫民以仁也，存心以公也，蒞事以勤也，此之謂四事，豈不以
translation_en:
…and the Book of Documents speaks of acting “as though protecting an infant.” This is precisely what is meant. The people of today are the same as the people of former times; the land of today is the same as the land of former times. Yet where formerly there was a reputation for abundance, today there are many impoverished households; where formerly the soil was praised as fertile, today there are many laments over abandoned fields. Why is the difference so great? Alas! I know the reason. The court establishes offices for the sake of the people, yet few officials entering office can serve the state faithfully. Compounding this are frequent natural calamities and the misery caused by local armed disturbances. How can one expect the land not to lie waste and the people not to suffer poverty? What, then, can be done? Must we not hold today’s officials responsible?

At the higher level, those entrusted with an entire region include the provincial administration commissioners and surveillance commissioners, each with their subordinate officials. At the lower level, those entrusted with a prefecture, subprefecture, or county include prefects and magistrates, who likewise each have subordinate officials. All these are called responsible officials, and upon them depend the well-being and suffering of the people. Can they fail to give this their attention? I have read the writings of Master Xishan and found therein a method for governing the people. When Xishan was in charge of Changsha, he urged his subordinates to strive in four matters and eliminate ten harmful practices. His words still survive today: are they not a guide and mirror for later generations? What he called disciplining oneself with integrity, caring for the people with benevolence, maintaining impartiality in one’s intentions, and attending to affairs with diligence—these are the four matters. Should they not be regarded as …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
爲美政而在所當勉者乎所謂斷獄不公
也聽訟不審也淹延囚繫也慘酷用刑也
泛濫追呼也招引告訐也重疊催稅也科
罰取財也縱吏下鄉也低價買物也此之
謂十害豈不以爲弊政而在所當去者乎
四事切於身心十害切於時弊西山雖爲
當時而言殆若爲今日而發有民社者聞
之能不惕然而興憮然而嘆者乎然以愚
者言之則又以四事爲本必先勉其四事
===
而後可以去其十害未有不勉四事而十
害可去者也吾見今之爲有司者其廉仁
公勤以愛民爲心者固多有之然亦有苞
苴入門而乏懸魚之操則持身不得爲廉
暴怒臨民而立吞𫔰之威則撫民不得爲
仁以媚竈之爲能嗤運甓之爲拙則又未
見其存心蒞事之公且勤也夫四事且未
能勉敢望其爲民去害哉抑十害之中則
尤有甚者夫刑獄死生繫于法而今也斷

punctuated:
爲美政而在所當勉者乎？所謂斷獄不公也，聽訟不審也，淹延囚繫也，慘酷用刑也，泛濫追呼也，招引告訐也，重疊催稅也，科罰取財也，縱吏下鄉也，低價買物也，此之謂十害，豈不以爲弊政而在所當去者乎？四事切於身心，十害切於時弊。西山雖爲當時而言，殆若爲今日而發。有民社者聞之，能不惕然而興，憮然而嘆者乎？然以愚者言之，則又以四事爲本，必先勉其四事，而後可以去其十害，未有不勉四事而十害可去者也。
吾見今之爲有司者，其廉仁公勤、以愛民爲心者，固多有之。然亦有苞苴入門而乏懸魚之操，則持身不得爲廉；暴怒臨民而立吞𫔰之威，則撫民不得爲仁；以媚竈之爲能，嗤運甓之爲拙，則又未見其存心蒞事之公且勤也。夫四事且未能勉，敢望其爲民去害哉？抑十害之中，則尤有甚者。夫刑獄死生繫于法，而今也斷
translation_en:
… regard these as good government and as practices in which one ought to exert oneself? What he calls deciding criminal cases unfairly, hearing lawsuits without careful inquiry, prolonging imprisonment, applying punishments cruelly, issuing summonses indiscriminately, encouraging accusations and denunciations, repeatedly pressing for taxes, exacting money through fines, allowing clerks free rein to enter the countryside, and buying goods at low prices—these are the ten abuses. Should these not be regarded as defective government and as practices that ought to be eliminated? The four duties bear directly upon one's person and mind; the ten abuses bear directly upon the evils of the times. Although Xishan spoke for his own day, his words seem almost to have been uttered for ours. Can those entrusted with the people and the local altars of soil hear them without being stirred to vigilance and sighing in dismay? Yet, in my humble view, the four duties are fundamental: one must first exert oneself in these four duties before one can eliminate the ten abuses. Never have the ten abuses been eliminated without diligence in the four duties.
I see that among officials today there are certainly many who are incorruptible, benevolent, impartial, and diligent, and whose hearts are set upon loving the people. Yet there are also those whose doors admit gifts and bribes, who lack the integrity exemplified by hanging up the fish to refuse further gifts; their personal conduct cannot be called incorruptible. Others confront the people in violent anger and establish a terrifying authority that threatens to devour them [?]; their care for the people cannot be called benevolent. They regard currying favor with the powerful—‘flattering the kitchen god’—as ability, and mock diligence—‘carrying bricks’—as clumsiness. In them, neither impartiality of intention nor diligence in handling affairs can be seen. If they cannot even exert themselves in the four duties, dare we expect them to remove abuses for the people? Moreover, among the ten abuses, some are especially grave. In criminal proceedings, life and death depend upon the law; yet nowadays, in deciding cases …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之不公用之慘酷者無枉
國法而恣爲則民命死於屠伯之手者多矣
財物多寡出於民而今也科罰取之低價
買之者雖招物議而罔顧則民利入於貪
夫之懷者亦多矣斯人也而可使之在民
上哉嗚呼爾俸爾祿民膏民脂下民易虐
上天難欺吾恐宋人戒石之銘未免爲官
府之文具也盍思
朝廷所以責成我者何如小民所以仰望我
===
者何如而我乃如是哉要當南面臨民之
時動以西山所言爲法首勉其四事以端
一身之本繼去其十害以除一時之弊又
當上與下而相孚彼與此而交勸爲長吏
者必以情達於下而不偃然以自尊爲僚
屬者必以情達於上而不退然以自處勉
所當勉如聖門之尊五美去所當去如聖
門之屏四惡至究其本則又在先有是愛
民之心然後可耳如是則庶幾所謂窮困

translation_en:
…those who adjudicate unfairly and apply punishments cruelly act wantonly in disregard of the laws of the state [?]. Thus many of the common people die at the hands of these butchers. Material resources, whether great or small in amount, come from the people. Yet nowadays those who seize them through fines or purchase them at low prices disregard public criticism even when they incur it. Thus much of the people's wealth also ends up in the pockets of greedy men. Can such men be allowed to stand above the people?

Alas! “Your salary and your emoluments are the people's fat and marrow. The people below are easily oppressed; Heaven above is hard to deceive.” I fear that this admonitory stone inscription of the Song has become mere official window dressing. Why do we not reflect on what the court expects us to accomplish and what the common people look to us for? How, then, can we behave like this?

Whenever we face south to govern the people, we must take Xishan's words as our rule in every action. First, we must strive to practice his four virtues, thereby setting right the foundation of our own conduct; next, we must eliminate his ten harms, thereby removing the abuses of our time. Superiors and subordinates must also trust one another, and each must encourage the other. Chief local administrators must communicate their true sentiments to those below, without arrogantly exalting themselves; subordinate officials must communicate their true sentiments to those above, without withdrawing into passivity. We must strive to practice what ought to be practiced, just as the school of the Sage honors the five excellent qualities; we must eliminate what ought to be eliminated, just as the school of the Sage rejects the four evils. Yet when we trace this to its root, it can be accomplished only if we first possess this heart that cherishes the people. In this way, we may approach what is meant by the saying, “Those in destitution…”

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者轉為富饒荒蕪者轉為沃壤上有以副
朝廷責成之意下有以慰斯民仰望之私而
天下美政至是成矣假令古之良吏如龔
黄卓魯者為今有司亦不過端治本清弊
源如西山所云者而已安有反古道拂人
情為斯民病哉方今
明天子在上視民如傷所以責成天下有司者
甚至而監臨有司者又有撫按諸憲臣焉
有司四事之能勉與否十害之能去與否
===
公論昭然自不可掩則歲首述職陟勸黜
懲固自有在愚生應有司而來姑因明問
論及之耳豈敢妄曰某也賢某也否以自
取出位之罪哉

punctuated:
者轉為富饒，荒蕪者轉為沃壤，上有以副朝廷責成之意，下有以慰斯民仰望之私，而天下美政至是成矣。假令古之良吏如龔、黄、卓、魯者為今有司，亦不過端治本、清弊源，如西山所云者而已，安有反古道、拂人情，為斯民病哉？
方今明天子在上，視民如傷，所以責成天下有司者甚至，而監臨有司者又有撫按諸憲臣焉。有司四事之能勉與否，十害之能去與否，公論昭然，自不可掩，則歲首述職，陟勸黜懲，固自有在。愚生應有司而來，姑因明問論及之耳，豈敢妄曰某也賢、某也否，以自取出位之罪哉？
translation_en:
…those in poverty will become prosperous, and wasteland will become fertile soil. Above, this will fulfill the court’s intention in holding officials responsible for results; below, it will satisfy the hopes that the people cherish. Good government throughout the realm will thereby be achieved. Were such fine officials of antiquity as Gong, Huang, Zhuo, and Lu serving as today’s administrative authorities, they would do no more than set right the foundations of government and eliminate the sources of abuses, just as Xishan said. How could they contravene the ancient Way and disregard human feelings, bringing suffering upon these people?
At present, our enlightened Son of Heaven reigns above, caring for the people as though they were injured. He is most exacting in holding the administrative authorities throughout the realm responsible for results. Moreover, Grand Coordinators and Regional Inspectors, all censorial officials, oversee those authorities. Whether officials diligently attend to the four duties, and whether they eliminate the ten abuses, are matters on which public judgment is clear and cannot be concealed. Thus, when they report on their service at the beginning of the year, there is assuredly a basis for promotion to encourage them and demotion to punish them. I, an unworthy student, have come in response to the authorities’ summons and have merely ventured to discuss these matters in answer to your discerning question. How would I dare rashly to declare that this man is worthy and that man is not, thereby bringing upon myself the offense of overstepping my station?

translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the guiyou year, the eighth year of Zhengde [1513], the time arrived for the Provincial Examinations throughout the realm. In the provinces, provincial officials conducted them according to established precedent and, once the proceedings were completed, submitted the examination records to the throne. Only in the two capitals did the prefectural officials, when the time arrived, request the appointment of Examiners, whom His Majesty specially commissioned, reflecting the importance attached to the capital regions. Thus your servants Yipeng and Long received the command to preside over the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination.

After taking leave of His Majesty and arriving at the examination compound, we found that the candidates had already gathered like clouds. The various officiating personnel and the artisans whose services were required had each been assigned to their respective offices and given instructions beforehand. All provisions for the examination compound, regulations, and indispensable safeguards [?] were fully in place. We were therefore able to devote ourselves wholeheartedly to evaluating the papers, seeking thereby to repay the imperial trust. Does this not make especially evident the depth of the ancestral emperors’ nurturing moral influence, and the manifest efficacy and great results of His Majesty’s honoring Confucian learning and esteeming the Way!” With a reverent bow, I have respectfully appended this preface to the final pages.
Now, in antiquity, men were employed as follows: those judged outstanding in the district schools were advanced to become ‘selected scholars’ (xuanshi); those judged outstanding by the Minister of Education (Situ) were advanced to become ‘eminent scholars’ (junshi); and those further judged outstanding by the Music Master-in-Chief (Da Yuezheng) were advanced to become ‘presented scholars’ (jinshi). Only then were they granted rank and emoluments. Today, scholars are nurtured in schools and selected through the examinations. Although the institutions may appear different, the intention remains the same insofar as men are assessed and selected by stages and brought into service. translation_en: …their talents and accomplishments stand out among their peers, just as grain plants put forth blossoms. When farmers sow grain, its first growth is the seedling; its flowering is called blossoming; and its production of grain is called bearing fruit. When scholars cultivate learning with reverence, humility, and constant diligence, enough to inspire awe in those who behold them, they resemble seedlings springing up vigorously. Once their self-cultivation has deepened, what has accumulated within increasingly flourishes in outward expression. Their accomplishments are then assessed, and the outstanding among them are honored as guests and recommended for advancement. This resembles grain plants rising into bloom, luxuriant with flowers and approaching maturity. Advancing without cease, their learning grows ever deeper and more abundant, sufficient for themselves and capable of benefiting others. They then enroll in service and pledge their allegiance, and are employed to govern the realm. This resembles grain that has filled out and ripened, ready to be harvested for food. Confucius said: “There are seedlings that never blossom! There are blossoms that never bear fruit!” Seedlings should blossom; if they do not, it is as though there had been no seedlings. Blossoms should bear fruit; if they do not, it is as though there had been no…

translation_en:
…having put forth no ears at all. Thus the farmer worries if his hundred mu remain untilled; he labors throughout the year and rests only when he has obtained grain to eat. The scholar worries if he has not attained the Way; he finds each day too short and rests only when his learning is complete and fit for practical use. There is a further point: the farmer seeks not merely grain, but prizes an abundant yield; the scholar seeks not merely accomplishment, but values greatness in accomplishment. Where this is not fully realized, it often depends on the place in which they are situated. Fields adjoining the city walls are to farmers what the capital, the foremost seat of moral excellence, is to scholars: no place takes precedence over these in pursuing abundance and greatness. Is this not because fertile soil is suited to planting and labor can readily be applied, while moral transformation reaches the capital first and its influence penetrates deeply?

translation_en:
…within the capital region lay the lands from which grain and rice were anciently supplied. In relation to the whole realm, this region resembles farmland adjoining a city’s outer walls. Like the wheat of Wen and the grain of Chengzhou, does it not invite high expectations? Those who flourish here should therefore gather in their blossoms and bring forth substantial fruit, presaging a plentiful harvest. Their yield should assuredly rank in the highest grade, beyond comparison with other lands. Thus may the people eat their fill and pat their contented bellies, singing of great peace, fulfilling our sagely Son of Heaven’s intention to nurture and bring repose to the common people. Would this not be magnificent?

But if they merely limit themselves to the glory of passing a single examination, remaining blind to aims more far-reaching and great, they willingly incur the ancient sage’s warning against flowering without bearing fruit. Their sowing achieves nothing; they are not even as good as weeds and barnyard grass. What, then, is worth seeking in their flowering? What is precious about fine seed? What is enviable about the excellence of farmland adjoining the city walls? 瀛臣祺皆遴選至自内臺其他
百執事亦皆慎簡以充而提調
内外則臣麃臣玥也宴既畢遂
以是日入院而六館諸司及列
郡應試之士凡二千八百有奇
punctuated: 朝廷所以待天下賢才，賢賢之道也。隨時緩急，一惟上命，乃輟所謂纂修者，即以求賢為重事。翌日，遂與臣龍進辭于廷，退宴于府。時同考試官學正臣大綱、臣大章、臣慈，教諭臣棠、臣嶽，訓導臣震、臣文榦、臣碩、臣衝，皆禮聘至自外郡。監試官監察御史臣瀛、臣祺，皆遴選至自内臺。其他百執事亦皆慎簡以充，而提調内外則臣庶、臣玥也。宴既畢，遂以是日入院。而六館諸司及列郡應試之士，凡二千八百有竒。
translation_en:
…is the means by which the court treats the worthy talents of the realm, the way of honoring the worthy. As circumstances and the urgency of affairs required, I followed solely His Majesty’s command. Thus I suspended the compilation work mentioned above and took seeking worthy men as my principal duty. The next day, together with your servant Long, I appeared at court to take leave, then withdrew to attend a banquet at the prefectural offices.

The Associate Examiners—instructors your servants Dagang, Dazhang, and Ci; instructors your servants Tang and Yue; and assistant instructors your servants Zhen, Wengan, Shuo, and Chong—had all been formally invited and had arrived from outlying prefectures. The examination monitoring officials, Investigating Censors your servants Ying and Qi, had both been carefully selected and had arrived from the Censorate. All the other functionaries had likewise been carefully chosen to fill their posts, while your servants Shu and Yue served as Proctors for affairs inside and outside the examination compound.

When the banquet was over, we entered the examination compound that same day. The candidates presenting themselves for examination from the Six Colleges, the various offices, and the several prefectures numbered more than two thousand eight hundred…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乃如故事三試之爰拔其尤得
百三十五人因錄其氏名幷文
之純者爲錄以
獻臣以職事宜爲序竊惟人才之
在天下其出而爲
國家用者類非一途然以
今日論之孰有重於科目者乎而
===
科目所取固以文耳故有司試
士與士之試于有司皆有不能
外是焉者顧其人學術有淺與
深則其造理有到與否其造理
有到與否則其措辭有高與下
文也者主乎理而達之辭者也
臣濫竽校文之任乃於

乃如故事三試之爰拔其尤得
百三十五人因錄其氏名并文
之純者爲錄以

在天下其出而爲
國家用者類非一途然以
今日論之孰有重於科目者乎而
===
科目所取固以文耳故有司試
士與士之試乎有司皆有不能
外是焉者顧其人學術有淺與
深則其造理有到與否其造理
有到與否則其措辭有高與下
文也者主乎理而達之辭者也
臣濫竽校文之任乃於
punctuated: 乃如故事三試之，爰拔其尤，得百三十五人。因錄其氏名，幷文之純者爲錄以獻。臣以職事宜爲序。竊惟人才之在天下，其出而爲國家用者，類非一途。然以今日論之，孰有重於科目者乎？而科目所取，固以文耳。故有司試士，與士之試于有司，皆有不能外是焉者。顧其人學術有淺與深，則其造理有到與否；其造理有到與否，則其措辭有高與下。文也者，主乎理而達之辭者也。臣濫竽校文之任，乃於
translation_en:
…Then, in accordance with established practice, we examined them in three sessions and selected the most outstanding, obtaining 135 men. We accordingly recorded their names and compiled their finest compositions into a record for presentation to the throne. By virtue of my official duties, it falls to your servant to write the preface.

I humbly reflect that talented men throughout the realm enter the service of the state by more than one path. Yet, speaking of the present day, what path carries greater weight than the civil-service examinations? And what the examinations select by is, indeed, written composition alone. Thus, both the officials who examine scholars and the scholars examined by those officials must work within this medium. Yet men’s learning may be shallow or deep, and accordingly they may or may not attain an understanding of principle; whether they attain such understanding determines whether their expression is elevated or low. Composition takes principle as its foundation and conveys it through words. Your servant, unworthily occupying the post of evaluating compositions, thereupon, among…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
京畿諸士之文得徧閱焉斐然成
章若皆有辭悠然趣味若皆有
理盖視天下為尤盛焉尤盛則
取之宜過於多而限於
制額則有弗得而盡然者亦惟窮
日夜殫心力務求其所謂高與
下者而甄別之其取其去一循
===
至公而不敢少以已意參焉以
仰副我
皇上求士之意此臣思竭駑鈍以求
逭其責者也雖然以文取士
朝廷立法然耳士之取重天下者
獨文乎哉昔孔子教人必兼文
行至論文學亦必以德行先之
alt_text:
京畿諸士之文得徧閱焉斐然成
章若皆有辭悠然趣味若皆有
理蓋視天下爲尤盛焉尤盛則
取之宜過於多而限於
制額則有弗得而盡然者亦惟竆
日夜殫心力務求其所謂高與
下者而甄别之其取其去一循
===
至公而不敢少以己意參焉以
仰副我
皇上求士之意此臣思竭駑鈍以求
逭其責者也雖然以文取士
朝廷立法然耳士之取重天下者
獨文乎哉昔孔子教人必兼文
行至論文學亦必以德行先之
punctuated:
京畿諸士之文，得徧閱焉。斐然成章，若皆有辭；悠然趣味，若皆有理。盖視天下為尤盛焉。尤盛，則取之宜過於多，而限於制額，則有弗得而盡然者。亦惟窮日夜，殫心力，務求其所謂高與下者而甄別之。其取其去，一循至公，而不敢少以已意參焉，以仰副我皇上求士之意。此臣思竭駑鈍，以求逭其責者也。
雖然，以文取士，朝廷立法然耳。士之取重天下者，獨文乎哉？昔孔子教人，必兼文行；至論文學，亦必以德行先之。
translation_en:
…I was able to read through the writings of the candidates from the metropolitan region. Elegantly composed, they all seemed accomplished in expression; with a lingering savor, they all seemed grounded in principle. Indeed, compared with those throughout the realm, these writings were especially outstanding. Such excellence would warrant selecting an exceptionally large number, but the prescribed quota prevented this from being fully realized. I could only labor day and night, exhausting my mental energies, striving to discern their relative merits and distinguish among them. In selecting or rejecting, I followed perfect impartiality alone, daring not to introduce the slightest personal preference, so as to fulfill our Emperor’s intention in seeking worthy men. This is how your servant has sought to expend his meager abilities and escape blame for failing in his responsibility.
Nevertheless, selecting men through their writing is simply the procedure established by the court. Is writing alone what earns a scholar the esteem of the realm? In former times, Confucius invariably combined literary learning with moral conduct in teaching others; even when discussing literary learning, he invariably placed virtuous conduct before it.

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖門所重盖如此諸士今以文
見録矣又將進而角天下士奉
廷對服官序寔自茲始盍使文行
彬彬實與華稱于以建偉績揚
休光蔚然成一代名臣而為天
下所取重乎夫是意也
朝廷所望於天下士者皆然況諸
===
士秀出
京畿固宜先天下而興者而可弗
知所重耶且臣輟纂修至此凡
以為
國家求賢也求而得人果如前所
云者則臣與有榮焉否則與有
愧焉臣用是懼乃敢輒附鄙意
alt_text:
聖門所重盖如此諸士今以文
見録矣又將進而角天下士奉
廷對服官序寔自茲始盍使文行
彬彬實與華稱于以建偉績揚
休光蔚然成一代名臣而爲天
下所取重乎夫是意也
朝廷所望於天下士者皆然况諸
===
士秀出
京畿固宜先天下而興者而可弗
知所重耶且〔臣〕輅纂修至此凡
以爲
國家求賢也求而得人果如前所
云者則〔臣〕與有榮焉否則〔臣〕與有
愧焉〔臣〕用是懼乃敢輒附鄙意
punctuated: 聖門所重盖如此。諸士今以文見録矣，又將進而角天下士，奉廷對，服官序，寔自茲始。盍使文行彬彬，實與華稱，于以建偉績，揚休光，蔚然成一代名臣，而為天下所取重乎？夫是意也，朝廷所望於天下士者皆然，況諸士秀出京畿，固宜先天下而興者，而可弗知所重耶？且臣輟纂修至此，凡以為國家求賢也。求而得人，果如前所云者，則臣與有榮焉；否則與有愧焉。臣用是懼，乃敢輒附鄙意
translation_en:
Such, indeed, were the priorities of the Sage’s school. You gentlemen have now been selected for your literary accomplishments. You will next advance to compete with scholars from throughout the realm, answer questions at court, and enter the ranks of official service: all this truly begins here. Why not bring your literary accomplishments and conduct into harmonious balance, making substance match outward refinement, so as to establish great achievements, spread the radiance of your virtue, and emerge as eminent ministers of your age, esteemed throughout the realm? Such are the court’s hopes for all scholars under Heaven. How much more does this apply to you gentlemen, who have distinguished yourselves in the capital region and ought indeed to rise ahead of the rest of the realm! Can you fail to understand what deserves importance?

Moreover, your servant suspended his compilation duties to come here solely to seek worthy men for the state. If those whom I seek and obtain truly prove to be as described above, then I shall share in their honor; otherwise, I shall share in their shame. This fills your servant with apprehension, and so I venture to append my humble thoughts…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
于末願與
京畿之士勉之且以勉天下之爲
士者固臣平日區區一念圖報
之誠也
翰林院侍講學士奉訓大夫吳
一鵬謹序

于末願與
京畿之士勉之且以勉天下之爲

之誠也
翰林院侍講學士奉訓大夫吳
一鵬謹序
punctuated:
于末，願與京畿之士勉之，且以勉天下之爲士者，固臣平日區區一念圖報之誠也。

翰林院侍講學士、奉訓大夫吳一鵬謹序。
translation_en:
…at the end, wishing to encourage the scholars of the capital region in this endeavor, and also to encourage all scholars throughout the realm. This, indeed, expresses your servant’s constant, humble sincerity in seeking to repay imperial favor.

Preface respectfully composed by Wu Yipeng, Expositor-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Instruction.

text:
第壹場
四書
十室之邑必有忠信如丘者焉不如丘之
好學也
可以贊天地之化育則可以與天地參矣
夫君子所過者化所存者神上下與天地
同流豈曰小補之哉
易
謙亨天道下濟而光明地道卑而上行天
===
道虧盈而益謙地道變盈而流謙鬼神
害盈而福謙人道惡盈而好謙謙尊而
光卑而不可踰君子之終也
初九利用爲大作元吉无咎
是故天生神物聖人則之
人謀鬼謀百姓與能
書
同寅協恭和衷哉
從諫弗咈先民時若

punctuated:
第壹場

四書

十室之邑，必有忠信如丘者焉，不如丘之好學也。

可以贊天地之化育，則可以與天地參矣。

夫君子所過者化，所存者神，上下與天地同流，豈曰小補之哉！

易

謙，亨。天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。天道虧盈而益謙，地道變盈而流謙，鬼神害盈而福謙，人道惡盈而好謙。謙，尊而光，卑而不可踰，君子之終也。

初九，利用爲大作，元吉，无咎。

是故天生神物，聖人則之。

人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。

書

同寅協恭，和衷哉！

從諫弗咈，先民時若。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“In a hamlet of ten households, there must be someone as loyal and trustworthy as I, Qiu; yet he will not equal my love of learning.”

“If one can assist the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth, one can then stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third.”

“Wherever the gentleman passes, people are transformed; wherever he abides, his influence is spirit-like. Above and below, he flows together with Heaven and Earth. How could one say that he offers merely a small benefit?”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“Modesty: success. The Way of Heaven sends its benefits downward and shines brightly; the Way of Earth occupies a low position, yet moves upward. The Way of Heaven diminishes the full and augments the modest; the Way of Earth alters the full and lets its benefits flow to the modest. Ghosts and spirits harm the full and bless the modest; the way of human beings is to dislike the full and favor the modest. Through modesty, those in high positions shine, while those in low positions cannot be overstepped. Thus does the gentleman carry things through to the end.”

“Initial nine: it is favorable to undertake great works. Supreme good fortune; no blame.”

“Therefore Heaven brings forth numinous things, and the sages take them as models.”

“Counsel is taken with men and with spirits, and the common people share in their efficacy.”

Book of Documents (Shujing)

“Be united in reverence, joined in respect, and harmonious at heart!”

“Follow remonstrance without resisting it, and conform to the worthy men of old.”

詩
緇衣之宜兮，敝，予又改爲兮。適子之館兮，還，予授子之粲兮。

translation_en:
It is said: reverence brings timely rain in due accordance; good governance brings timely sunshine in due accordance.
Do not say, “I cannot”; rather, exert your heart to the utmost. Do not say, “The people are few”; rather, attend carefully to their affairs.

The Book of Odes
How well the black robes suit you! When they wear out, I will make them anew. I go to your lodging; when you return, I will give you food.
A bundle of fresh-cut fodder; that man is like jade.
Like flight, like soaring wings; like the Yangtze, like the Han; like a mountain’s luxuriant growth, like a river’s flow.
Unceasingly diligent and reverent, he cannot be fathomed or overcome.
Is he not illustrious, is he not worthy of honor? Never does he weary of serving others.

The Spring and Autumn Annals
Shu of Xiao paid court to the duke. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The grandees and the women of the ruling lineage presented themselves, using silk as gifts. 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
The men of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕 The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed; they then attacked Chu. Qu Wan of Chu came to the army to conclude a covenant; they concluded the covenant at Shaoling. 〔Both in the fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
The men of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, and the Baron of Xu besieged Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xi.〕
The Marquis of Jin invaded Cao. The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei. The Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, and the army of Song…

Discourse

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
曉然知臣虜之爲非而遂奉我
聖祖爲中國主嗚呼大哉
皇言何其感應神速若是哉今去之百五十年
而中原父老尚有能莊誦而弗忘者則
在當時可知已抑可得而聞其槩乎往
時漢伐秦唐伐隋宋受周禪皆號以治
易亂然未聞檄諭天下者何也豈亦有
之而今不傳乎抑有不待於檄諭也竊
觀是檄所載雖爲諭告一時臣民而發
===
要之帝王治天下之道實不外此我
聖祖匪徒言之實允蹈之固以之定天下訓萬
世矣豈非
聖子神孫所當世世欽承而傳之無疆者乎夫
堯言萬世如見而所謂燕薊者即今
京畿地也諸生生長於斯游歌於斯諒必稔
聞之矣其敬述以對
問聖賢之道措之而爲政事發之而爲文
章未嘗無所本也先儒有謂禮樂政事

punctuated:
曉然知臣虜之爲非，而遂奉我聖祖爲中國主。嗚呼，大哉皇言！何其感應神速若是哉！今去之百五十年，而中原父老尚有能莊誦而弗忘者，則在當時可知已。抑可得而聞其槩乎？往時漢伐秦，唐伐隋，宋受周禪，皆號以治易亂，然未聞檄諭天下者，何也？豈亦有之而今不傳乎？抑有不待於檄諭也？竊觀是檄所載，雖爲諭告一時臣民而發，要之，帝王治天下之道實不外此。我聖祖匪徒言之，實允蹈之，固以之定天下、訓萬世矣。豈非聖子神孫所當世世欽承而傳之無疆者乎？夫堯言萬世如見，而所謂燕薊者，即今京畿地也。諸生生長於斯，游歌於斯，諒必稔聞之矣。其敬述以對。

問：聖賢之道，措之而爲政事，發之而爲文章，未嘗無所本也。先儒有謂禮樂政事
translation_en:
…clearly understood that serving the foreign captors as subjects was wrong, and thereupon acclaimed our Sagely Progenitor as ruler of China. Ah, how great were these imperial words! How could they have elicited so swift and wondrous a response! Now, a hundred and fifty years later, there are still elders of the Central Plain who can solemnly recite them without forgetting them; from this we may judge their effect at the time. Might we hear an account of their substance? In earlier times, Han attacked Qin, Tang attacked Sui, and Song received the throne through Zhou’s abdication. All claimed to replace disorder with good government, yet we have heard of no proclamations issued by them to instruct all under Heaven. Why is this? Did such proclamations also exist, but fail to survive to the present? Or did their circumstances not require proclamations?

On examining the contents of this proclamation, I find that, although it was issued to instruct the subjects of that time, in essence the way by which emperors and kings govern all under Heaven lies entirely within it. Our Sagely Progenitor did not merely speak these words: he truly put them into practice. Indeed, through them he pacified all under Heaven and instructed ten thousand generations. Is this not something that his sagely sons and divine grandsons should reverently receive, generation after generation, and transmit without end? The words of Yao remain as vividly present through ten thousand generations as if he stood before us; and the places called Yan and Ji are precisely the present metropolitan region. You students were born and raised here, and here you have pursued your studies and sung your songs. Surely you must be thoroughly familiar with this proclamation. Reverently recount it in your answers.

Question: The Way of the sages and worthies, when put into practice, becomes affairs of government; when expressed in words, it becomes literary composition. It has never lacked a foundation. An earlier Confucian scholar said that rites, music, and affairs of government…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不可不出于一有謂文章道德不可使
出於二其亦各有所見乎三代之後世
未甞無禮樂也何以謂之虛名禮樂不
可斯須去身而謂百年而後興者無乃
迂與諸葛亮治蜀汲汲以興復為事他
固未遑及也曰孔明庶幾禮樂其旨安
在漢有君甞擬作大章矣所以任之者
果后夔其人乎唐有君甞欲行周禮矣
其為輔相者果周公其人乎其治效竟
===
何如也六經之後世未甞無文章也何
以謂之無益有德者必有言而謂文章
與時高下不亦遠與揚子雲於漢每每
以詞賦為工餘尚有可議也曰揚雄庶
幾於道其意何居唐有儒稱其師以為
得周公孔子之趣可矣而因文見道何
以猶有譏乎宋有儒贊其師以為得文
王孔子之傳似矣而終身行事何以尚
有疵乎其議論果孰是也請詳著于篇

出於二其亦各有所見乎三代之後世
未嘗無禮樂也何以謂之虛名禮樂不
可斯須去身而謂百年而後興者無乃

固未遑及也曰孔明庶幾禮樂其旨安

果后夔其人乎唐有君嘗欲行周禮矣
其爲輔相者果周公其人乎其治效竟
何如也六經之後世未嘗無文章也何
以謂之無益有德者必有言而謂文章
與時高下不亦遠與揚子雲於漢每每
以詞賦爲工餘尚有可議也曰揚雄庶
幾於道其意何居唐有儒稱其師以爲
得周公孔子之趣可矣而因文見道何
以稱有識乎宋有儒贊其師以爲得文
王孔子之傳似矣而終身行事何以尚
有疵乎其議論果孰是也請詳著于篇
punctuated: 不可不出于一；有謂「文章道德不可使出於二」。其亦各有所見乎？三代之後，世未甞無禮樂也，何以謂之虛名？禮樂不可斯須去身，而謂百年而後興者，無乃迂與？諸葛亮治蜀，汲汲以興復為事，他固未遑及也。曰「孔明庶幾禮樂」，其旨安在？漢有君甞擬作大章矣，所以任之者，果后夔其人乎？唐有君甞欲行周禮矣，其為輔相者，果周公其人乎？其治效竟何如也？六經之後，世未甞無文章也，何以謂之無益？有德者必有言，而謂文章與時高下，不亦遠與？揚子雲於漢，每每以詞賦為工，餘尚有可議也。曰「揚雄庶幾於道」，其意何居？唐有儒稱其師，以為得周公、孔子之趣，可矣；而因文見道，何以猶有譏乎？宋有儒贊其師，以為得文王、孔子之傳，似矣；而終身行事，何以尚有疵乎？其議論果孰是也？請詳著于篇，
translation_en:
…must proceed from a single source; another has said, “Literary composition and moral virtue must not be allowed to proceed from two separate sources.” Did each of these statements reflect a particular insight? After the Three Dynasties, the world was never without rites and music. Why, then, were they called empty names? Rites and music cannot be absent from one’s person even for a moment; is it not impractical to say that they can flourish only after a hundred years? When Zhuge Liang governed Shu, he devoted himself urgently to restoring the Han and indeed had no leisure for other matters. What, then, is the purport of the statement, “Kongming came close to realizing rites and music”? A Han ruler once proposed to create the Great Manifestation music. Was the man entrusted with this task truly another Hou Kui? A Tang ruler once wished to implement the Rites of Zhou. Was the man serving as his chief minister truly another Duke of Zhou? What, in the end, were the results of their government?

After the Six Classics, the world was never without literary composition. Why, then, was it called useless? Those who possess virtue necessarily have something to say; is it not a considerable departure from this to say that literary composition rises and falls with the times? Yang Ziyun of the Han repeatedly displayed his skill in verse and rhapsodies, while other aspects of his work remained open to criticism. What is meant, then, by the statement, “Yang Xiong came close to the Way”? A Confucian scholar of the Tang praised his teacher as having grasped the purport of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. This may be acceptable; yet why was there still criticism of discerning the Way through his writings? A Confucian scholar of the Song praised his teacher as having received the transmitted teachings of King Wen and Confucius. This seems plausible; yet why were faults still found in his conduct throughout his life? Which of these judgments is actually correct? Please set out your views in detail in your essay…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
觀所以潤身而及物者
問孔子謂君子疾沒世而名不稱孟子又
謂聲聞過情君子所恥則名固君子所
尚而亦不可無實盜名正以天下後世
公論難掩故也簡冊所載私相稱謂者
多矣姑舉其一二相類者試以問焉有
當春秋末報讎襄子至擊其衣然後為
快而稱之為真義士者有當漢文時屯
軍細柳至遏乘輿然後令行而稱之為
===
真將軍者有輔相中興識兵畧達時令
而稱之為真漢相者有出刺豫州舉阿
縱脩政事而稱之為真刺史者有當國
儲之議立而不以利怵威懼存諸心而
稱之為真社稷臣者有因故主之歸欵
而不表獻其土地以求利而稱之為真
純臣者有議事延英破太平可樂之諛
辭而稱之為真宰相者有奉使雲中全
萬里銜命之節操而稱之為真忠臣者

punctuated:
觀所以潤身而及物者。

問：孔子謂君子疾沒世而名不稱，孟子又謂聲聞過情，君子所恥，則名固君子所尚，而亦不可無實盜名，正以天下後世公論難掩故也。簡冊所載，私相稱謂者多矣。姑舉其一二相類者，試以問焉。有當春秋末，報讎襄子，至擊其衣然後為快，而稱之為真義士者；有當漢文時，屯軍細柳，至遏乘輿然後令行，而稱之為真將軍者；有輔相中興，識兵畧，達時令，而稱之為真漢相者；有出刺豫州，舉阿縱，脩政事，而稱之為真刺史者；有當國儲之議立，而不以利怵、威懼存諸心，而稱之為真社稷臣者；有因故主之歸欵，而不表獻其土地以求利，而稱之為真純臣者；有議事延英，破太平可樂之諛辭，而稱之為真宰相者；有奉使雲中，全萬里銜命之節操，而稱之為真忠臣者；
translation_en:
…to see how one cultivates oneself and extends the benefits to others.

Question: Confucius said that the gentleman grieves at reaching the end of his life without his name being commended. Mencius also said that a reputation exceeding one's actual merits is something the gentleman regards as shameful. Thus reputation is indeed something the gentleman values, yet he must not steal a reputation without possessing the substance to support it. This is precisely because the public judgment of the world and of later generations is difficult to suppress. The historical records contain many instances of people privately praising one another. Let us select a few similar examples and put them to you as a question.

There was one who, at the end of the Spring and Autumn period, sought vengeance against Xiangzi and was satisfied only after striking his clothing; he was praised as a true man of righteousness. There was one who, during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, stationed his troops at Xiliu and enforced his orders even to the point of halting the imperial carriage; he was praised as a true general. There was one who assisted the restoration of the dynasty as chief minister, understood military strategy, and comprehended the ordinances appropriate to the seasons; he was praised as a true Han chancellor. There was one who went out to serve as Regional Inspector of Yuzhou, recommended A Zong [?], and put government affairs in order; he was praised as a true Regional Inspector. There was one who, when the establishment of an heir apparent was being debated, allowed neither enticement by gain nor fear of coercion to enter his heart; he was praised as a true minister of the state. There was one who, when his former lord submitted, did not seek personal advantage by presenting a memorial offering up that lord's territory; he was praised as a truly incorruptible minister. There was one who, while discussing affairs in the Yanying Hall, refuted the flattering claim that peace and prosperity could simply be enjoyed; he was praised as a true chief minister. There was one who, sent on a mission to Yunzhong, maintained the integrity of an imperial envoy across ten thousand li; he was praised as a truly loyal minister…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有身居宰輔論事有先見而稱之爲真
聖人者有身任言責直聲動四方而稱
之爲真御史者有建儲草詔筆不輕下
而稱之爲真學士者有經筵進講一時
聳聽而稱之爲真侍講者有三人貢獻
不市上恩而總稱之爲真良吏者有一
人奇偉見重於時而兼稱之爲真宰相
真男子者凡此皆君子美稱或出於一
時之褒嘉或得之後世之追論而真之
===
爲言又非形似彷彿之謂以今觀之信
乎其難也已抑不知之數人者果足以
當是名而無愧歟抑有名浮其實者存
其間也願明以告我且觀尚友之志毋
諉之曰不暇
問夫人幼而學之壯而欲行之此古今不
易之理也三代以上其人之見于事功
澤被當時芳流後世者未有不本於學
術漢以来乃有不盡然者姑舉數子相
alt_text:
有身居宰輔論事有先見而稱之爲真
聖人者有身任言責直聲動四方而稱
之爲真御史者有建儲草詔筆不輕下
而稱之爲真學士者有經筵進講一時
聳聽而稱之爲真侍講者有三人貢獻
不市上恩而總稱之爲真良吏者有一
人奇偉見重於時而無稱之爲真宰相
真男子者凡此皆君子美稱或出於一
時之褒嘉或得之後世之追論而真之
===

乎其難也已抑不知之數人者果足以
當是名而無愧歟抑有名浮其實者存

punctuated:
有身居宰輔，論事有先見，而稱之爲真聖人者；有身任言責，直聲動四方，而稱之爲真御史者；有建儲草詔，筆不輕下，而稱之爲真學士者；有經筵進講，一時聳聽，而稱之爲真侍講者；有三人貢獻，不市上恩，而總稱之爲真良吏者；有一人奇偉，見重於時，而兼稱之爲真宰相、真男子者。凡此皆君子美稱，或出於一時之褒嘉，或得之後世之追論。而真之爲言，又非形似彷彿之謂。以今觀之，信乎其難也已！抑不知之數人者，果足以當是名而無愧歟？抑有名浮其實者存其間也？願明以告我，且觀尚友之志，毋諉之曰不暇。
問：夫人幼而學之，壯而欲行之，此古今不易之理也。三代以上，其人之見于事功，澤被當時，芳流後世者，未有不本於學術。漢以来，乃有不盡然者。姑舉數子相
translation_en:
…There was one who occupied the position of chief minister, showed foresight in discussing affairs, and was called a true sage; one who bore responsibility for remonstrance, whose reputation for forthrightness stirred the four quarters, and who was called a true censor; one who drafted an edict establishing the heir apparent, would not lightly set brush to paper, and was called a true academician; and one who lectured at the Classics Colloquium, commanded the attention of all present, and was called a true expositor-in-waiting. There were three men who presented tribute without seeking to purchase the sovereign’s favor and were collectively called true good officials. There was also one man of extraordinary stature, esteemed in his time, who was called both a true chief minister and a true man. All these are laudatory appellations for exemplary men: some arose from praise bestowed in their own time, while others were acquired through the retrospective judgments of later generations. Yet the word “true” does not signify merely an outward likeness or an approximate resemblance. Viewed from the present, how difficult it surely is to merit such a designation! Still, I wonder whether these several men [?] really deserved these names without shame, or whether some among them enjoyed reputations exceeding their actual merits. Please explain this clearly to me, so that I may also discern your aspiration to take the ancients as friends. Do not excuse yourselves by saying that you lack the time.
Question: People study in youth and, upon reaching maturity, wish to put what they have learned into practice. This is a principle unchanged from antiquity to the present. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, those whose achievements were manifest in public affairs, whose beneficence reached their contemporaries, and whose good name endured in later generations invariably grounded their accomplishments in learning. Since the Han, however, this has not always been so. Let us provisionally cite a few men and together…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
與論其世可乎重厚少文者木強之人
耳何以能副大事之屬卒建社稷之功
不學無術者匹夫之類耳何以能受託
孤之詔以成伊周之業或謂其人之似
光而顛沛之中飲博自如摧強敵於談
笑之頃或謂其人之似勃而危疑之際
不動聲色措國家於泰山之安不知其
為學術者果亦各有所類故其設施若
合符節抑其天資偶合有不在於學術
===
耶或謂之有儒者氣象或謂之非知學
不能當時未見其果何所學而為帝師
為謀臣其建立卓然為一代之冠而明
經對策立談封侯者顧曲學阿世無救
於海內虛耗之弊有其學止於論語一
部者有以論語終身誦之者當時未聞
其別有所學而任天下之重得大臣之
體其相業炳然非後世可及而博學強
記致位宰輔者乃變亂成法使天下喪
