translation_en:
…[The opening phrase 莫如 is unclear: ?], just as the four seasons follow their constant, unchanging course and the myriad kinds of beings attain fulfillment. People naturally sustain their own lives, forgetting what enables them to do so: this is simply the circulation of genuine virtue. Can those who fulfill their promises and receive benefits from others on that account really regard this as trustworthiness? Households naturally maintain themselves, forgetting what enables them to do so: this is simply the state expressed in “What has the emperor’s power to do with me?” Can those who remember longstanding pledges and whose households receive rewards on that account truly be spoken of in these terms? Ah! The fulfillment of desires does not arise from asking; the bestowal of virtue demands no repayment. Such was what the ancients called trustworthiness!

Generally, all requests arise from insufficiency, while receiving something does not necessarily leave one with a surplus. To regard this as trustworthiness is already to concern oneself with its least important aspects. Could the instances in which it falls short of trustworthiness ever be counted? As for the Way of the sage, the myriad beings depend upon it for life, and it does not refuse them; it loves and nourishes them without acting as their master. It may be called great, yet it never claims greatness, and thus it can fulfill its greatness. Fish stranded on land moisten one another with their mouths and wet one another with foam. They certainly show diligence and affection, but this cannot equal the greatness of swimming in rivers and lakes, forgetting who has made this possible. From this we may understand what makes trustworthiness truly trustworthiness: the ancients, as it were, forgot one another in the rivers and lakes; later generations merely lie stranded on land, moistening and wetting one another. This too is something readers of the Book of Rites should understand.

Discourse

“Learning What Master Yan Learned”

Shi Dao

text:
同考試官訓導周批論題平易場中誰不
知亦誰不能作但多汎而不切間有立論稍奇者便
失恠僻殊不愜意晩得此卷議論閎深神采迅發而
性理之學明敏之才具於篇中見之豈亦學顏而有
得者耶起敬起敬
同考試官教諭吳批論塲士子類能言之
詞險者失之怪意深者失之鑿此卷議論精確筆力
雄健奇寓於純粹巧藏於和易菽粟之味布帛之文
具眼者讀之自見豈可以文士目之耶春闈魁薦吾
===
尚於子有望焉

詞昌大之氣發聖賢之學金精玉粹又宛然顏子口中
語也學識如是豈特可冠秋闈而已耶

translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor: The discourse topic is straightforward. Who in the examination hall does not understand it, and who cannot write on it? Yet most responses are vague and fail to address it closely. Occasionally, an argument shows some originality, only to lapse into strangeness and eccentricity, leaving one thoroughly dissatisfied. Late in the reading I came upon this paper: its argument is broad and profound, its spirit flashes forth, and both learning in human nature and principle and an intelligent, discerning talent are evident throughout. Could its author, too, have gained something from studying Yan Zi? My respect is stirred—my respect is stirred!

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Candidates in the discourse examination can generally discuss this subject. Those whose wording is adventurous err through oddity; those whose ideas aim at profundity err through forced interpretation. This paper argues with precision and certainty, and its writing is vigorous and powerful. Originality resides within purity, and skill is concealed within harmony and ease. It has the savor of beans and grain, the texture of cloth and silk: discerning readers will recognize these qualities for themselves. How could its author be regarded merely as a literary man? I still hope to see you recommended at the head of the spring Metropolitan Examination.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Mentor: Learning from the sages begins with Yan Zi; learning from Yan Zi begins with mastering oneself. The moment an argument departs from this, it is no longer discussing Yan Zi. This composition alone brings forth the learning of the sages and worthies through language that follows classical standards and a spirit of expansive grandeur. Refined as gold and pure as jade, it seems, moreover, to consist of words spoken by Yan Zi himself. With learning and discernment such as these, could its author merely rank first in the autumn Provincial Examination?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Expositor-in-waiting: Nowadays, candidates writing discourses often marshal empty phrases that crowd the paper in profusion while having no connection whatsoever with the actual topic. This paper alone integrates the commentary on the Book of Penetration (Tongshu) into a coherent composition. It has force of expression, insight into principle, and disciplined form: an excellent discourse. The expectation that its author should be raised above all the other candidates is indeed well founded.

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
學以聖人為至聖人不可以易學也學其幾聖
人者斯可矣幾乎聖人則所造固已聖域辦在
守與化之間其為聖人甚易易耳顏子以聖人
為可至也學其所以為聖人者而幾聖人固其
所也故善學聖人莫如顏子而學聖人者必自
顏子始則有以得入聖之階而學庶乎其不差
矣不然必有非其學而學者不可以為學也不
可以為學其可以為士乎其可以希賢而希聖
以至於天乎請因周子之言而論之學也者所
===
以造乎道而求至其極也道至於聖人天下之
所謂學者宜無出其右矣而聖人猶有學焉士
非賢有士之學所以學為賢也賢非聖有賢人
之學所以學為聖也聖人欲何為哉道之大原
出於天唯聖人為能體之其心未以為足而欲
與天為一也故學其為天至於天則有以窮道
之原不可以復加矣若是則士之為學亦求至
乎聖人而已其何以希賢為哉聖人未有盛於
孔子者亦學孔子而已其何以顏子為哉聖人

punctuated:
學以聖人為至，聖人不可以易學也。學其幾聖人者，斯可矣。幾乎聖人，則所造固已聖域，辦在守與化之間，其為聖人甚易易耳。顏子以聖人為可至也，學其所以為聖人者，而幾聖人固其所也。故善學聖人莫如顏子，而學聖人者必自顏子始，則有以得入聖之階，而學庶乎其不差矣。不然，必有非其學而學者，不可以為學也。不可以為學，其可以為士乎？其可以希賢而希聖，以至於天乎？請因周子之言而論之。

學也者，所以造乎道而求至其極也。道至於聖人，天下之所謂學者宜無出其右矣，而聖人猶有學焉。士非賢，有士之學，所以學為賢也；賢非聖，有賢人之學，所以學為聖也。聖人欲何為哉？道之大原出於天，唯聖人為能體之，其心未以為足，而欲與天為一也，故學其為天。至於天，則有以窮道之原，不可以復加矣。若是，則士之為學亦求至乎聖人而已，其何以希賢為哉？聖人未有盛於孔子者，亦學孔子而已，其何以顏子為哉？聖人
translation_en:
Learning takes sagehood as its ultimate attainment, yet a sage cannot easily be emulated. One may, however, emulate someone who has come close to sagehood. Someone close to sagehood has already reached the realm of the sages; the distinction lies between holding fast and becoming transformed [?], and becoming a sage is then very easy indeed. Yan Zi regarded sagehood as attainable and studied what makes a sage a sage; approaching sagehood was thus his natural attainment. Hence no one excelled Yan Zi at emulating the sages. Those who would emulate the sages must begin with Yan Zi: they will then find the steps by which to enter sagehood, and their learning may avoid going astray. Otherwise, they will inevitably pursue studies other than those they ought to pursue, which cannot count as learning. If this cannot count as learning, can they count as scholars? Can they aspire to become worthies, then sages, and ultimately attain to Heaven? Allow me to discuss this on the basis of Zhou Zi’s words.

Learning is the means by which one advances in the Way and seeks to reach its utmost limit. When attainment in the Way reaches sagehood, surely none of those whom the world calls learners should surpass it; yet even sages still have learning to undertake. A scholar is not yet a worthy: there is the learning proper to scholars, by which they learn to become worthies. A worthy is not yet a sage: there is the learning proper to worthies, by which they learn to become sages. What, then, does a sage seek to become? The great source of the Way issues from Heaven, and only a sage can embody it. Yet in his heart he does not consider this sufficient and wishes to become one with Heaven; thus he learns to become like Heaven. Upon attaining to Heaven, he can fully fathom the source of the Way, and nothing further can be added. If so, scholars in their learning likewise seek only to attain sagehood. Why, then, must they aspire to become worthies? Among sages, none has surpassed Kong Zi; one need only emulate Kong Zi. What need, then, is there for Yan Zi? A sage…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不可以遽學也於是而學賢人以賢人去聖人
不遠由賢人以至聖人可也非舍聖人而弗之
學學賢人固所以學聖人也孔子不可以遽學
也於是而學顏子以顏子去孔子不遠由顏子
以至孔子可也非舍孔子而弗之學學顏子固
所以學孔子也顏子何以去孔子不遠而學孔
子者必欲學之乎觀其所以為仁可見矣所聞
纔數言爾而至明有以察其幾至健有以致其
决非禮則勿視也非禮則勿聽也非禮則勿言
===
也非禮則勿動也此其克己復禮為顏子之所
以學者乎及其有得焉不能無怒怒則不為之
遷不能無過過則不為之貳不能無違於仁仁
則三月而不違其學如此而已矣何以為善學
孔子耶孔子所以聖者渾然天理而已彼見其
所以渾然者而欲學焉故其潜心如此爾己者
私也有以害其渾然者故必克之禮者理也即
所謂渾然者故必復之怒而不遷此理之發於
情者不能蕩而鑿也過而不貳此理之接於物

…cannot be emulated all at once. One therefore learns from worthy men: since worthy men are not far removed from sages, one can proceed through the worthy to reach sagehood. This does not mean setting sages aside and declining to learn from them; learning from the worthy is precisely the means of learning from sages. Confucius cannot be emulated all at once. One therefore learns from Master Yan: since Master Yan is not far removed from Confucius, one can proceed through Master Yan to reach Confucius. This does not mean setting Confucius aside and declining to learn from him; learning from Master Yan is precisely the means of learning from Confucius.

Why was Master Yan not far removed from Confucius, and why must those who learn from Confucius seek to learn from him? This can be seen by examining how he practiced humaneness. What he heard amounted to only a few words, yet his utmost clarity enabled him to discern their subtle implications, and his utmost strength enabled him to carry his resolve through: do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not speak what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not act contrary to ritual propriety. Was this overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety not the way Master Yan pursued learning? When he had attained something through it, he could not be entirely without anger, but when angry he did not transfer his anger to others. He could not be entirely without faults, but when he erred he did not repeat the fault. He could not be entirely without departures from humaneness, but he could remain without departing from it for three months. His learning amounted to this alone. Why, then, is he considered to have excelled in learning from Confucius?

What made Confucius a sage was simply the undivided wholeness of heavenly principle. Master Yan perceived what constituted that wholeness and wished to learn it; hence his wholehearted application was like this. The self means selfishness: it can impair that wholeness, and therefore must be overcome. Ritual propriety is principle itself, the very wholeness just mentioned, and therefore must be restored. To be angry without transferring one’s anger means that this principle, as it manifests in the emotions, cannot be dissipated or impaired. 也已其從此理而無所用其力矣乎觀夫群弟
子之中藝則有矣達則有矣果則有矣聰明才
辨又無不有矣有如顏子潛心聖人若此其篤
者乎此其獨為好學而幾于聖人也自夫管商
===
之徒出則有功利其學者矣申韓之徒出則有
刑名其學者矣儀秦之徒出則有從橫其學者

足為甚病也乃若所謂士者則固當以孔子為
學者也柰之何號為孔子之徒而實非所以學
孔子也廣見聞焉失之汗漫而不知守其約工

自夫管商之徒出，則有功利其學者矣；申韓之徒出，則有刑名其學者矣；儀秦之徒出，則有從橫其學者矣；楊墨佛老之徒出，則又有異端其學者矣。豈復知有孔門之所謂學者哉？豈復知有顏子而學其學者哉？然而尚幸以非吾儒之道，其是非邪正之相形，不啻黑白，而天下皆曉然能辨，不足為甚病也。乃若所謂士者，則固當以孔子為學者也。柰之何號為孔子之徒，而實非所以學孔子也？廣見聞焉，失之汗漫而不知守其約；工
translation_en:
…cannot be drawn away and lost. His not departing from benevolence for three months means that he held fast to the principle attained through neither transferring his anger nor repeating his faults, but had not yet become fully transformed by it. He extended it further and developed it through analogous cases. That he “delighted in everything” means that, on hearing this principle, he immediately understood it inwardly; that he “was also able to bring it to light” means that, having grasped this principle, he immediately put it to the test in his own experience; that “when spoken to, he was never slack” means that, understanding this principle, he immediately exerted himself to practice it. “Though I wished to stop, I could not”: was this because his delight in this principle would not let him stop? “There is no way to do so”: was this because, in following this principle, he had reached a point where there was no means of applying further effort? Among the other disciples, there were those accomplished in the arts, those of sound judgment, and those of resolution; intelligence, ability, and eloquence were all to be found among them. Yet was there anyone who devoted his mind to emulating the Sage as earnestly as Master Yan? This is why he alone was deemed to love learning and came close to being a sage.

Once the followers of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang appeared, some made achievement and profit their learning. Once the followers of Shen Buhai and Han Fei appeared, some made punishments and administrative accountability their learning. Once the followers of Zhang Yi and Su Qin appeared, some made the forging of vertical and horizontal alliances their learning. Once the followers of Yang Zhu, Mo Di, the Buddha, and Laozi appeared, others made heterodox teachings their learning. How could they still know what the school of Confucius called learning? How could they still recognize Master Yan and learn as he learned? Fortunately, however, these teachings lay outside the Way of us Confucians. The contrast between right and wrong, deviant and correct, was as distinct as black and white, and everyone in the world could clearly distinguish them; thus they did not constitute a very grave affliction. But those called scholars surely ought to take Confucius as their model in learning. How is it that they call themselves followers of Confucius, yet in practice fail to learn from him? They broaden what they see and hear, but fall into boundless diffuseness and do not know to hold fast to the essentials; they cultivate skill…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
文辭焉失之浮華而不知求其實矜智能焉失
之誇詐而不知習其誠慕空寂焉失之荒唐而
不知養其正是而爲學則亦何補於身心何闗
於至理亦何以爲士而希聖賢之道哉故爲學
則必學聖人學聖人則必學顏子學顏子則亦
克己復禮而已宥弗視視必以禮非禮者彼不
視也吾其敢視乎有弗聽聽必以禮非禮者彼
不聽也吾其敢聽乎有弗言言必以禮有弗動
動必以禮非禮者彼不言不動也吾其敢言敢
===
動乎於是觀其爲怒不遷與否遷則非其學也
必不遷而後已察其爲過不貳與否貳則非其
學也必不貳而後已驗其爲仁不違與否違則
非其學也必不違而後已之其無所不說而求
其說者何如之其亦足以發而求其發者何如
之其語而不惰而求其不惰者何如將欲罷也
則曰彼猶竭才我其可以不竭乎將欲從也則
曰彼猶末由我其何以爲由乎心齋坐忘是學
也何爲而廣聞見終日如愚是學也何爲而工

曰彼猶未由我其何以為由乎心齋坐忘是學
也何為而廣聞見終日如愚是學也何為而工
punctuated: 文辭焉，失之浮華而不知求其實；矜智能焉，失之誇詐而不知習其誠；慕空寂焉，失之荒唐而不知養其正。是而爲學，則亦何補於身心？何闗於至理？亦何以爲士而希聖賢之道哉？故爲學則必學聖人，學聖人則必學顏子，學顏子則亦克己復禮而已。宥弗視，視必以禮，非禮者彼不視也，吾其敢視乎？有弗聽，聽必以禮，非禮者彼不聽也，吾其敢聽乎？有弗言，言必以禮；有弗動，動必以禮。非禮者彼不言不動也，吾其敢言敢動乎？於是觀其爲怒不遷與否，遷則非其學也，必不遷而後已；察其爲過不貳與否，貳則非其學也，必不貳而後已；驗其爲仁不違與否，違則非其學也，必不違而後已。之其無所不說，而求其說者何如；之其亦足以發，而求其發者何如；之其語而不惰，而求其不惰者何如。將欲罷也，則曰：「彼猶竭才，我其可以不竭乎？」將欲從也，則曰：「彼猶末由，我其何以爲由乎？」心齋坐忘，是學也，何爲而廣聞見？終日如愚，是學也，何爲而工
translation_en:
…literary language, they lapse into superficial ornament and do not know to seek substance; priding themselves on their intelligence and abilities, they lapse into boastfulness and deceit and do not know to practice sincerity; admiring emptiness and stillness, they lapse into wild absurdity and do not know to cultivate rectitude. If this is what they call learning, how does it benefit body and mind? What connection does it have with ultimate principle? How, moreover, can they thereby become scholars and aspire to the Way of the sages and worthies? Thus, in learning one must take the sage as one’s model; to learn from the sage, one must learn from Master Yan; and to learn from Master Yan is simply to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety. There are things one must not look at [?]; whenever one looks, it must accord with ritual propriety. He would not look at what was contrary to ritual propriety: would I dare look at it? There are things one must not listen to; whenever one listens, it must accord with ritual propriety. He would not listen to what was contrary to ritual propriety: would I dare listen to it? There are things one must not say; whenever one speaks, it must accord with ritual propriety. There are actions one must not perform; whenever one acts, it must accord with ritual propriety. He would neither speak nor act contrary to ritual propriety: would I dare speak or act thus?

Accordingly, examine whether you refrain from transferring your anger to others. If you do transfer it, yours is not his learning; you must persist until you no longer do so. Scrutinize whether you refrain from repeating your faults. If you repeat them, yours is not his learning; you must persist until you no longer do so. Test whether you remain unwavering in benevolence. If you depart from it, yours is not his learning; you must persist until you no longer do so. Consider [?] how he delighted in everything he was taught, and inquire into the nature of that delight; consider [?] how he was also able to illuminate the teaching, and inquire into the nature of that illumination; consider [?] how, when spoken to, he was never indolent, and inquire into the nature of that diligence. When about to give up, say: “He still exerted his abilities to the utmost; can I fail to exert mine?” When wishing to follow, say: “Even he had no way to do so; by what means can I find a way?” Fasting of the mind and sitting in forgetfulness—this is learning; why, then, broaden what one hears and sees? Appearing foolish all day long—this is learning; why, then, devote oneself to crafting…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
文辭無伐善無施勞是學也何為而矜知能擇
乎中庸是學也何為而慕空寂然則顏子以學
孔子而謂之好學我其不以學顏子而為好學
乎顏子以好學幾於孔子我其不以好學而幾
於顏子乎向嘗美求之藝也今則求失其能矣
何有於管商向嘗羨賜之達也今則賜失其辯
矣何有於儀秦向嘗慕由之决也今則由失其
勇矣何有於申韓向嘗多諸弟子之聰明才辯
也今則皆有以失其所長矣又何有於楊墨佛
===
老者哉其用之也則以四代禮樂而與顏子同
其行其舍之也則以簞瓢陋巷而與顏子同其
藏學至於是則亦庶乎其顏子矣夫顏子所以
不為聖人者守之也非化之也假之以年不日
而化矣則化而為聖人者固非顏子所難也吾
患弗能守耳至於能守則化非所患矣吾患弗
為顏子耳至於顏子則為孔子非所患矣至於
孔子則渾然太極之妙合天人而為一不知所
謂孔子不知所謂為天亦不知所謂為我如此

punctuated: 文辭？無伐善，無施勞，是學也，何為而矜知能？擇乎中庸，是學也，何為而慕空寂？然則顏子以學孔子而謂之好學，我其不以學顏子而為好學乎？顏子以好學幾於孔子，我其不以好學而幾於顏子乎？向嘗美求之藝也，今則求失其能矣，何有於管商？向嘗羨賜之達也，今則賜失其辯矣，何有於儀秦？向嘗慕由之决也，今則由失其勇矣，何有於申韓？向嘗多諸弟子之聰明才辯也，今則皆有以失其所長矣，又何有於楊墨佛老者哉？其用之也，則以四代禮樂而與顏子同其行；其舍之也，則以簞瓢陋巷而與顏子同其藏。學至於是，則亦庶乎其顏子矣。夫顏子所以不為聖人者，守之也，非化之也。假之以年，不日而化矣，則化而為聖人者，固非顏子所難也。吾患弗能守耳，至於能守，則化非所患矣。吾患弗為顏子耳，至於顏子，則為孔子非所患矣。至於孔子，則渾然太極之妙，合天人而為一，不知所謂孔子，不知所謂為天，亦不知所謂為我。如此
translation_en:
…polish literary expression? Not boasting of one’s goodness and not making a display of one’s meritorious labors—this is learning. Why, then, take pride in knowledge and ability? Choosing the Mean—this is learning. Why, then, yearn for emptiness and stillness? If Master Yan was called a lover of learning because he learned from Kongzi, should I not become a lover of learning by learning from Master Yan? If Master Yan approached Kongzi through his love of learning, should I not approach Master Yan through a love of learning?

Formerly I admired Qiu’s accomplishments, but now even Qiu (Ran Qiu) has lost his claim to ability; what standing, then, have Guan Zhong and Shang Yang? Formerly I envied Ci’s discernment, but now even Ci (Duanmu Ci) has lost his claim to eloquence; what standing, then, have Zhang Yi and Su Qin? Formerly I admired You’s decisiveness, but now even You (Zhong You) has lost his claim to courage; what standing, then, have Shen Buhai and Han Fei? Formerly I esteemed the intelligence, talent, and eloquence of the various disciples, but now all have grounds for losing their claims to their particular strengths. What standing, then, have Yang Zhu, Mo Di, the Buddha, and Laozi?

When employed in office, one would put into practice the rites and music of the four dynasties, sharing Master Yan’s course of action. When set aside, one would live with a basket of rice and a gourd of water in a humble lane, sharing Master Yan’s withdrawal. When learning reaches this point, one comes close to being a Master Yan.

The reason Master Yan had not become a sage was that he held fast to his attainment but had not yet undergone transformation. Had he been granted more years, he would before long have been transformed. Transformation into a sage was certainly no difficult matter for Master Yan. My concern is only that I cannot hold fast; once I can hold fast, transformation will be no cause for concern. My concern is only that I cannot become a Master Yan; once I reach Master Yan’s level, becoming a Kongzi will be no cause for concern. Upon reaching Kongzi’s level, there is the undivided subtlety of the Supreme Ultimate, uniting Heaven and humanity as one. One no longer knows what is meant by Kongzi, what is meant by being Heaven, or what is meant by being oneself. Only thus …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然後為學之至而不可以復加矣惜夫顏子未
及為聖人未及為天而徒為希聖希天者之準
的也此孔子所以深嘆其不幸矣乎嗚呼顏子
之不幸萬世學者之幸也孔子之不可以易至
尚矣有顏子則人皆知希聖之有準的用功有
所持循自能尋向上去而孔子可至也故曰過
則聖及則賢不及則亦不失於令名必然之理
也微夫顏氏之子則遂謂聖人為不可學悵悵
乎莫知所之其不惑於他岐者幾希夫子開萬
===
世道學之源而顏子梯航接引之功亦不可誣
也濂溪以是為訓其亦善學顏子者歟其亦善
學孔子者歟

然後為學之至，而不可以復加矣。惜夫！顏子未及為聖人，未及為天，而徒為希聖希天者之準的也。此孔子所以深嘆其不幸矣乎！嗚呼！顏子之不幸，萬世學者之幸也。孔子之不可以易至，尚矣。有顏子，則人皆知希聖之有準的，用功有所持循，自能尋向上去，而孔子可至也。故曰：「過則聖，及則賢，不及則亦不失於令名。」必然之理也。微夫顏氏之子，則遂謂聖人為不可學，悵悵乎莫知所之，其不惑於他岐者幾希！夫子開萬世道學之源，而顏子梯航接引之功，亦不可誣也。濂溪以是為訓，其亦善學顏子者歟？其亦善學孔子者歟？

蔣承恩

同考試官訓導于批〔將順中有責難意，忠〕
translation_en:
…only then does learning reach its utmost, beyond which nothing further can be added. What a pity! Master Yan did not live to become a sage or to become one with Heaven, but served only as the standard for those aspiring to sagehood and to Heaven. Was this why Kongzi so deeply lamented his misfortune? Alas! Master Yan’s misfortune is the good fortune of learners for ten thousand generations. That Kongzi’s level cannot easily be attained has long been recognized. With Master Yan as an example, everyone knows that aspiration to sagehood has a standard; they have something to follow and hold to in their efforts, and can naturally find their way upward until Kongzi’s level becomes attainable. Thus it is said: “Those who surpass him become sages; those who equal him become worthies; even those who fall short will not fail to earn a good name.” This is an inevitable principle. Without the son of the Yan family, people would conclude that sagehood could not be learned. Despondent and knowing nowhere to turn, how few would avoid being led astray down other paths! The Master opened the source of the Learning of the Way for ten thousand generations; nor can Master Yan’s achievement in providing the ladders and boats to guide others onward be denied. In making this his teaching, was Lianxi not also skilled at learning from Master Yan? Was he not also skilled at learning from Kongzi?

Memorial

臣某等言：伏覩慶曆四年春正月，皇上復御經筵者，臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言。伏以緝熙帝學，得升高行遠之資；涵養聖心，為端本澄源之地。故朝廷講筵之設，寔天下治忽所關，豈玩空文？欲求至道。先朝創舉，屢收啓沃之功；聖志欽承，克念始終之典。蠢兹元昊，忽勞西顧之憂；惡比有苗，尚梗中邦之治。睿算方勤于帷幄，神功暫輟於殿庭。天啓戎衷，誠輸欵塞；帝敷文德，化格舞階。世方有為，賛可忘乎冊籍？

〔…the utmost devoted love. It should be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner Liu, Left Rectifier, comments: 〔Full yet disciplined, ornate yet elegant: it captures the style of Song memorials.〕
Examiner Wu, Academician Expositor-in-waiting, comments: 〔This congratulatory memorial is classically elegant and skillfully emulates the language of Song writers. Accept it.〕
Your servants, So-and-so and others, state: We have reverently observed that in the first month of spring in the fourth year of Qingli, Your Majesty resumed attendance at the Classics Colloquium. With heartfelt joy and delight, we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow as we submit this memorial.
We humbly consider that bringing ever greater brilliance to imperial learning provides the means to ascend to heights and travel far; nurturing the sagely mind lays the foundation for rectifying the root and clearing the source. Thus the court’s establishment of lectures bears directly upon order or disorder throughout the realm. Could it be mere dalliance with empty words? Its purpose is to seek the highest Way. The preceding reign instituted this practice and repeatedly reaped the benefits of enlightening the sovereign’s mind. Your Majesty reverently carried forward that intention, mindful of maintaining the institution from beginning to end.
Then this rebellious Yuanhao suddenly burdened you with anxiety over the western frontier. His wickedness rivaled that of the Youmiao, and he continued to obstruct good government in the Central Realm. While your sagacious calculations occupied the command tent, your divine work in the palace hall was temporarily suspended. Heaven opened the hearts of the western tribes, and they sincerely submitted at the frontier gates. The emperor spread civil virtue, and its transforming influence reached them, as when dances were performed before the palace steps. In an age ripe for accomplishment, could the assistance afforded by books be forgotten? [?] …

translation_en:
…With your mind intent upon taking no ease, lectures were accordingly urged by the Confucian ministers. This excellent institution has now been restored, and sounds of rejoicing spread throughout the Four Seas. Civil culture gains stature, and military achievements acquire further lustre. We reverently consider that ○○○○: your consummate nature was formed early, and your outstanding gifts were divinely bestowed. Matching the glory of the founding ancestor, you magnificently inherit an unshakable foundation; showing filial devotion to the Grand Emperor [?], you widely extend the transforming influence of renewal. Personally practising benevolence and frugality, you bring about great peace without exertion.
Your perfect sincerity reaches Heaven’s heart above; your sagely virtue finds expression below in songs of praise. You should daily renew yourself through inquiry and study, thereby inspiring all within the realm. The classics and histories record past and present, and emperors and kings draw upon them through lectures and study. punctuated: 天聽於九重，退朝習以為常，盛暑樂而忘倦。以道心為一身之主，知君德為萬化之原。盖惟書可以維持此心，若非學，何以懋隆其德？涓流不擇，而後效可期；一簣或虧，則前功盡棄。惟宸衷之素定，致聖學之大成。發而為仁義道德之言，措則成雍熙泰和之治。是固非泥篇章之陳迹，而寔有得精一之真傳者也。臣某等幸際昌期，快瞻盛事，臨木天而致慶，望學海以颺言。徒懷野人曝背之忱，殊乏大臣格心之術。尚冀乾行不息，謙道有終，業求益精于勤，心不自以為聖。四夷歸化，仰中國之有聖人；一德感孚，見滿朝之皆君子。臣某等無任瞻
translation_en:
…your imperial hearing within the ninefold palace. After court, you make study your regular practice; even in the height of summer, you delight in it and forget weariness. You make the moral mind the master of your whole person, knowing that the ruler’s virtue is the source of all transformation. Indeed, only books can sustain this mind; without learning, how could one further exalt that virtue? Only by rejecting no tiny stream can eventual achievement be expected; if even one basketful of earth is lacking, all previous effort is thrown away. Through the longstanding resolve of your imperial heart, your sagely learning reaches its full accomplishment. Expressed in words, it becomes discourse on benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue; put into practice, it produces harmonious and peaceful government. This assuredly is no clinging to the stale traces of written compositions: it is truly to have received the authentic transmission of refinement and single-mindedness.

We, your servants So-and-so and the others, are fortunate to live in this flourishing age and rejoice to witness this splendid undertaking. Approaching the “wooden heaven,” the imperial literary precinct, we offer congratulations; gazing toward the ocean of learning, we raise our voices in praise. We possess only the sincerity of the rustic who would offer his sovereign the pleasure of warming his back in the sun; we utterly lack the great minister’s art of rectifying the ruler’s heart. Yet we hope that, like Heaven in its course, you will never cease your exertions, and that you will follow the way of humility to its completion; that through diligence you will seek ever greater mastery in your endeavors, and that in your heart you will never deem yourself already a sage. The peoples of the four quarters will submit to your transforming influence, looking up in admiration that the central realm has a sage; your undivided virtue will move them to trust, and they will see that your court is filled entirely with gentlemen. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, cannot contain our feelings as we gaze upward…

考試官侍講學士吳批：我聖祖得天下，以立萬世不拔之業，其大在辨華夏、正綱常，二者具見是檄中。故首舉為問，尊聖製也。場中能荅者甚少，獨此策鋪張揚厲，辭贍氣昌。末復言列聖、今上與祖宗先後同心圖治，尤為有識。畿甸竒士，吾不於子望而誰望哉？
translation_en:
…The essay on the imperial composition is especially remarkable in its portrayal of divine achievements surpassing those of ancient emperors and kings. Once it is engraved and displayed throughout the realm, will there not be those who, like men of old, draw upon it to compose a eulogy of imperial virtue?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Companion of the Heir Apparent: This proclamation reveals why Heaven’s mandate and the hearts of the people abandoned the non-Chinese Yuan and turned to our sagely founding ancestor. It also amply attests to the loftiness and brilliance of his sagely learning and the vastness of his divine achievements. Everything that his sagely sons and divine grandsons throughout the ages ought grandly to inherit as the basis of their government is contained here as well. This policy essay expounds these matters almost exhaustively. At its close, it further praises the flourishing preservation of the inherited achievement today, thereby expressing loyalty and devotion. Its author may well be called a man of exceptional discernment. We include it in this record to provide a model for future students.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Expositor-in-Waiting: Our sagely founding ancestor won the realm and established an unshakable foundation for all ages. His greatness lay in distinguishing Hua-Xia civilization from outsiders and rectifying the cardinal bonds and constant moral norms. Both are fully apparent in this proclamation. We therefore made it the subject of the first question, to honor the imperial composition. Very few in the examination hall could answer it. This policy essay alone expansively celebrates its subject, with abundant diction and vigorous spirit. At its close, it further states that the successive sage emperors and His present Majesty have shared with their imperial ancestors, generation after generation, a single resolve to achieve good government. This shows particular discernment. For an outstanding scholar of the metropolitan region, if I do not look to you, to whom should I look?

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
皇言出於一時而有以感天下之人心
帝業傳於萬世而有以隆天下之治化夫人心
之感本於
皇言之誠治化之隆本於
帝業之大此可見我
太祖高皇帝之創業垂統為萬世計者過於古
帝王遠矣嗚呼天下有大界限華夷是也
天下有大道理綱常倫紀是也元以夷狄
竊據中華者九十餘年所謂大界限者至
===
是盡隳所謂大道理者至是盡壞盖自古
中國被夷狄之毒未有若此甚者嗚呼此
何等時耶我
聖祖挺生南服順
天應人天戈所向靡不克捷首取江南以繫天
下之人心繼都金陵以據天下之形勝而
天下之歸
聖祖者可坐而定也顧中原之人間有冥迷而
弗悟者故不得已而馳檄諭之愚嘗聞之

punctuated:
皇言出於一時，而有以感天下之人心；帝業傳於萬世，而有以隆天下之治化。夫人心之感，本於皇言之誠；治化之隆，本於帝業之大。此可見我太祖高皇帝之創業垂統，為萬世計者，過於古帝王遠矣。
嗚呼！天下有大界限，華夷是也；天下有大道理，綱常倫紀是也。元以夷狄竊據中華者九十餘年，所謂大界限者至是盡隳，所謂大道理者至是盡壞。盖自古中國被夷狄之毒，未有若此甚者。嗚呼！此何等時耶？我聖祖挺生南服，順天應人，天戈所向，靡不克捷。首取江南，以繫天下之人心；繼都金陵，以據天下之形勝，而天下之歸聖祖者，可坐而定也。顧中原之人，間有冥迷而弗悟者，故不得已而馳檄諭之。愚嘗聞之
translation_en:
Imperial words are uttered at a particular moment, yet can move the hearts of all under Heaven; the imperial enterprise is transmitted through ten thousand generations, yet can elevate governance and moral transformation throughout the realm. The moving of hearts is rooted in the sincerity of imperial words; the flourishing of governance and moral transformation is rooted in the greatness of the imperial enterprise. From this we can see how our Emperor Taizu Gao, in founding his enterprise and bequeathing the dynastic succession, planned for ten thousand generations far beyond the emperors and kings of antiquity.
Alas! There is a great boundary under Heaven: that between the Chinese and the barbarians. There are great moral principles under Heaven: the cardinal bonds, constant virtues, and ordered human relationships. The Yuan, being barbarians, usurped possession of the Chinese heartland for more than ninety years. By then, that great boundary had been utterly demolished, and those great moral principles utterly destroyed. Since antiquity, China had never suffered such grievous harm from barbarians. Alas! What a time this was! Our sagely founder arose preeminent in the southern regions, obeying Heaven and responding to the people. Wherever his heavenly weapons were directed, he invariably won victory. First he took Jiangnan, thereby securing the allegiance of all under Heaven; then he established his capital at Jinling, thereby occupying the realm’s strategically commanding terrain. The allegiance of all under Heaven to our sagely founder could thus be assured with ease. Yet among the people of the Central Plain there were still some who remained benighted and failed to awaken. He therefore had no choice but to dispatch a proclamation to instruct them. I, in my ignorance, once heard of this …

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
遺老參之國史而仰窺其一二矣請得而
敬陳之檄之大畧有曰自古帝王臨御天
下中國居內以制夷狄夷狄居外以奉中
國未聞夷狄居中國治天下如元者也斯
言也所以斥元之汚我華夏而嚴天下之
大界限也又曰元有天下之後廢壞綱常
廢長立幼戕君酖兄至於弟收兄妻子烝
父妾上下相習恬不爲怪斯言也所以斥
元之壞我名教而正天下之大道理也其
===
後又曰中原氣盛當生聖人驅逐胡虜恢
復中華拯生民於塗炭覩漢官之威儀斯
言也又所以斥元之閏數既盡而示天下
之大氣運也至理本於
聖心之斡運而非矯飾於目前妙思出於
聖筆之揮洒而非假手於臣下其詞直其氣壯
嗚呼其誠哉於是中原之人一聞
皇言如寐而寤如醉而醒悔臣虜之爲非知從
華之爲正而天下歸

punctuated:
遺老，參之國史，而仰窺其一二矣。請得而敬陳之。檄之大畧有曰：「自古帝王臨御天下，中國居內以制夷狄，夷狄居外以奉中國，未聞夷狄居中國治天下如元者也。」斯言也，所以斥元之汚我華夏，而嚴天下之大界限也。又曰：「元有天下之後，廢壞綱常，廢長立幼，戕君酖兄，至於弟收兄妻，子烝父妾，上下相習，恬不爲怪。」斯言也，所以斥元之壞我名教，而正天下之大道理也。其後又曰：「中原氣盛，當生聖人，驅逐胡虜，恢復中華，拯生民於塗炭，覩漢官之威儀。」斯言也，又所以斥元之閏數既盡，而示天下之大氣運也。
至理本於聖心之斡運，而非矯飾於目前；妙思出於聖筆之揮洒，而非假手於臣下。其詞直，其氣壯。嗚呼，其誠哉！於是中原之人一聞皇言，如寐而寤，如醉而醒，悔臣虜之爲非，知從華之爲正，而天下歸
translation_en:
…from surviving elders, and, checking it against the dynastic history, have reverently gained some small understanding of it. Allow me respectfully to set it forth. The proclamation says, in its broad outline: “Since ancient times, when emperors ruled all under Heaven, the Central Kingdom occupied the interior to control the barbarians, while the barbarians occupied the exterior to serve the Central Kingdom. Never have we heard of barbarians occupying the Central Kingdom and ruling all under Heaven as the Yuan have done.” These words condemn the Yuan for defiling our Huaxia civilization and firmly establish the great boundary dividing the world. It also says: “After the Yuan came to possess all under Heaven, they cast aside and ruined the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. They displaced the elder and enthroned the younger, murdered their rulers and poisoned their elder brothers. Younger brothers even took their elder brothers’ wives, and sons had illicit relations with their fathers’ concubines. High and low followed one another in these practices, complacently finding nothing strange in them.” These words condemn the Yuan for ruining our moral teachings and rectify the great principles governing all under Heaven. Later it also says: “The vital energy of the Central Plains is flourishing; a sage is destined to arise, to drive out the barbarian foes, restore the Central Kingdom, rescue the people from utter misery, and behold the dignified bearing of Han officials.” These words further denounce the Yuan as having exhausted the allotted span of their illegitimate rule, and reveal the great movement of Heaven’s fortune throughout the world.
The highest principles arose from the workings of the sagely mind, rather than being contrived for appearances at the moment; the marvelous conceptions flowed from the sweep of the sagely brush, rather than being entrusted to subordinate officials. The language is forthright, its spirit mighty. Ah, how sincere it is! Thus, as soon as the people of the Central Plains heard the imperial words, they were like sleepers awakening or drunkards becoming sober. They regretted the wrong of serving the barbarians as subjects and recognized the rightness of giving allegiance to Chinese civilization, and all under Heaven gave allegiance to…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
聖祖者如建瓴然未幾遂拾宋掇秦掣趙拔燕
天命歸而
帝業成矣謂非是檄亦有助哉灭除隋之亂太
宗所以爲唐受周之禪藝祖所以爲宋然
未聞檄諭天下者何也則以彼皆中國代
中國而綱常固自在也若秦爲西戎韓淮
陰且有馳檄三秦之說則漢高亦嘗用之
特未及於天下耳况壞我綱常如胡元者
哉又嘗竊窺是檄矣
===
宸翰汪洋所包甚廣施之臣民則爲諭告之
詞施之帝王則爲致治之道有可得而言
者誠以人君爲斯民宗主朝廷爲天下根
本而所以爲御世之防者則惟禮義而已
所謂禮義孰有大於華夷之限隔乎又孰
大於綱常倫紀之不瀆乎
聖祖於御極之初即立萬世之法外而控制夷
狄也則因元主北遁之後慎固邊防責之
將帥於其貢琛而歸化者綏之以德如舜

將帥於其貢琛而歸化者綏之以德如弈
punctuated:
聖祖者，如建瓴然。未幾，遂拾宋掇秦，掣趙拔燕，天命歸而帝業成矣。謂非是檄亦有助哉？灭除隋之亂，太宗所以爲唐；受周之禪，藝祖所以爲宋。然未聞檄諭天下者，何也？則以彼皆中國代中國，而綱常固自在也。若秦爲西戎，韓淮陰且有馳檄三秦之說，則漢高亦嘗用之，特未及於天下耳。况壞我綱常如胡元者哉？又嘗竊窺是檄矣。
宸翰汪洋，所包甚廣。施之臣民，則爲諭告之詞；施之帝王，則爲致治之道。有可得而言者：誠以人君爲斯民宗主，朝廷爲天下根本，而所以爲御世之防者，則惟禮義而已。所謂禮義，孰有大於華夷之限隔乎？又孰大於綱常倫紀之不瀆乎？聖祖於御極之初，即立萬世之法。外而控制夷狄也，則因元主北遁之後，慎固邊防，責之將帥；於其貢琛而歸化者，綏之以德，如舜
translation_en:
…to the Sagely Founder as irresistibly as water pouring from a tilted vessel. Before long, he gathered in Song and Qin, seized Zhao, and took Yan; the Mandate of Heaven came to him, and his imperial enterprise was accomplished. Could one say that this proclamation did not also contribute? Suppressing the disorders of Sui was how Taizong established Tang; receiving Zhou’s abdication was how the Founding Ancestor established Song. Yet we hear of no proclamation issued by either to instruct all under Heaven. Why? Because in both cases one Chinese dynasty replaced another, and the cardinal bonds and constant virtues remained intact. As for Qin, it belonged to the western Rong; even Han Xin, the Marquis of Huaiyin, spoke of dispatching a proclamation to the Three Qin. Thus Gaozu of Han also employed this means, though he did not extend it to all under Heaven. How much more necessary was it against the foreign Yuan, who destroyed our cardinal bonds and constant virtues! I have also ventured to examine this proclamation further.
The imperial writing is vast and expansive, encompassing a very broad range. Applied to subjects and people, it provides words of instruction and admonition; applied to emperors and kings, it provides the way to achieve good government. Something can be said of this: truly, the ruler is the sovereign lord of the people, and the court is the foundation of all under Heaven; yet the safeguards by which the world is governed consist solely in ritual propriety and righteousness. Within what we call ritual propriety and righteousness, what is greater than the boundary separating Chinese and foreigners? And what is greater than keeping the cardinal bonds, constant virtues, and ordered human relationships inviolate? At the very beginning of his reign, the Sagely Founder established rules for all generations. In external affairs, to keep the foreign peoples under control after the Yuan ruler fled north, he carefully strengthened the frontier defenses and charged his generals with their protection. Those who offered precious objects as tribute and submitted to his civilizing influence he pacified through virtue, like Shun…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之格有苗也執迷而弗悛者懾之以威如
禹之征有扈也而天下之大界限始嚴內
而撫循中國也則因元政汚染之餘申明
禮制責之有司於明倫而爲善良者教以
五倫如虞之命契也亂倫而爲敝民者弼
以五刑如虞之任臯陶也而天下之大道
理始正挈二帝三王已淪之疆土而還我
中國舉二帝三王已壞之綱常而還我人
民前有以承萬年
===
寶曆之正傳後有以創
一代金甌之大業天冠地履之分截如也鳳
儀獸舞之治煕如也天下化成至矣盡矣
嗚呼休哉
太宗文皇帝繼體於後又欲以南化北也徙元
舊都兩京並建盖自開闢以来所發之王
氣至是始足當之而所以禦外安內者寔
與
聖祖而同心

而撫循中國也則因元政汚染之餘申明
禮制責之有司於明倫而爲善良者教以
五倫如虞之命契也亂倫而爲敝民者癸
以五刑如虞之任臯陶也而天下之大道
理始正挈二帝三王已淪之疆土而還我
中國舉二帝三王已壞之綱常而還我人
民前有以承萬年
===
寶曆之正傳後有以創
一代金甌之大業天冠地屨之分截如也鳳
儀獸舞之治熙如也天下化成至矣盡矣
嗚呼休哉
太宗文皇帝繼體於後又欲以南化北也徙元
舊都兩京並建盖自開闢以來所發之王
氣至是始足當之而所以禦外安內者寔
與
聖祖而同心
punctuated:
之格有苗也。執迷而弗悛者，懾之以威，如禹之征有扈也，而天下之大界限始嚴。內而撫循中國也，則因元政汚染之餘，申明禮制，責之有司。於明倫而爲善良者，教以五倫，如虞之命契也；亂倫而爲敝民者，弼以五刑，如虞之任臯陶也，而天下之大道理始正。挈二帝三王已淪之疆土而還我中國，舉二帝三王已壞之綱常而還我人民。前有以承萬年寶曆之正傳，後有以創一代金甌之大業。天冠地履之分，截如也；鳳儀獸舞之治，煕如也。天下化成，至矣，盡矣！嗚呼，休哉！
太宗文皇帝繼體於後，又欲以南化北也，徙元舊都，兩京並建。盖自開闢以来所發之王氣，至是始足當之。而所以禦外安內者，寔與聖祖而同心。
translation_en:
…bringing the Youmiao to submission. Those who persisted in their delusion and would not repent he awed with his might, as Yu did when campaigning against the Youhu [?]; only then was the great boundary dividing all under Heaven strictly maintained. Within, in caring for and pacifying the central realm, he addressed the lingering corruption of Yuan government by reaffirming the ritual institutions and charging the responsible officials with their enforcement. Those who understood human relationships and became good people he instructed in the five human relationships, as the ruler of Yu did when appointing Xie. Those who disrupted human relationships and became corrupt members of the populace he corrected with the five punishments, as the ruler of Yu did when employing Gao Yao. Only then were the great moral principles of all under Heaven set right. He recovered the lost territories of the Two Emperors and Three Kings and restored them to our central realm; he revived their ruined cardinal bonds and constant norms and restored them to our people. Looking backward, he continued the orthodox transmission of the imperial succession through the myriad years; looking forward, he founded the great enterprise of a dynasty as whole and secure as a golden bowl. The distinction between Heaven above, like a cap, and Earth below, like shoes, was sharply defined; the harmonious government under which phoenixes appeared in stately array and beasts danced shone forth. The moral transformation of all under Heaven reached its utmost perfection and completeness. Ah, how glorious!
Emperor Taizong Wen succeeded him and further sought to transform the north through the influence of the south. He moved the capital to the former Yuan capital, establishing the two capitals side by side. Only then did a ruler fully match the kingly energies that had arisen there since the separation of Heaven and Earth. In his means of defending against external threats and securing peace within, he was indeed of one mind with the Sacred Founder.

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承益隆治道逮我
皇上繼述彌光而所以禦外安内者又與
聖祖
文皇而同心當是時也無怠無荒四夷来王不
識不知順帝之則雖有匡時如管仲者不
得施攘夷之功憂時如賈生者無以發風
俗之嘆而我
國家大氣運之隆殆與天地相為悠久而無
疆矣愚敢拜手稽首為
===
今日賀
第二問
史道
同考試官訓導周批策有考據有斷制條

translation_en:
The successive sage emperors inherited the throne and further advanced the way of good government. With our present Emperor, the continuation of their work has become still more glorious; in repelling external threats and securing peace within, he shares the intentions of the Sagely Founder and Emperor Wen. In this age there is neither indolence nor neglect, and the barbarians of the four quarters come to acknowledge his sovereignty; without conscious knowledge or awareness, the people follow the Supreme Lord’s pattern. Even someone as capable of setting his age right as Guan Zhong would have no occasion to achieve merit by driving out the barbarians; someone as concerned for his age as Master Jia would have no cause to lament prevailing customs. The flourishing fortune of our dynasty may thus endure as long as Heaven and Earth, without limit. I humbly venture to bow with clasped hands and knock my head to the ground, offering congratulations on this day.

text:
先儒定論具在場中士子類能言之而援據精當敷答
詳明者僅見此篇噫子之潤身及物其亦有合一之可
觀歟
考試官侍講學士吳批此篇據先儒成說隨問隨
答筆端沛然了無凝滯平素其究心理學者歟
爲治必有其實而不可以名求爲文必有
其本而不可以末務治以名求具焉而已
雖美何裨文以末務辭焉而已雖工何補
禮樂治之實也見於施爲必此道之充周
===
然後足以化民而成俗道德文之本也形
于制作必此理之暢達然後足以名世而
傳遠是治固不可不出於一而文亦豈可
出於二哉夫功成作樂治定制禮三代以
還世未嘗無禮樂也何歐陽子例以爲虛
名乎盖聖人之禮樂不越起居動作之間
而寓夫殊事合敬之道不出經世宰物之
典而得乎異文同愛之機叔侯所謂禮以
行政是也後世則以行於朝廷奏於郊廟

translation_en:
…The settled conclusions of earlier Confucian scholars are all available, and most candidates in the examination hall can state them. Yet this essay alone cites evidence with precision and aptness and develops its answers fully and clearly. Ah! In cultivating yourself and benefiting others, might you likewise display a unity worthy of admiration?
Examiner Wu, Academician Expositor, comments: This essay draws on the established teachings of earlier Confucian scholars, answering each question in turn. Its writing flows abundantly, without the slightest obstruction. Must its author not have devoted himself habitually to the study of principle?
Governing must have substance; it cannot be pursued through mere names. Writing must have a foundation; it cannot be practiced by attending only to its incidental features. When government is pursued through names, there is nothing but its apparatus: however splendid, what benefit does it bring? When writing attends only to incidental features, there is nothing but words: however skillful, what use are they? Rites and music are the substance of government. When manifested in practical action, this Way must pervade everything before it can transform the people and establish good customs. The Way and virtue are the foundation of writing. When embodied in literary composition, this principle must find full and unimpeded expression before the writing can win renown in its age and be transmitted to distant posterity. Thus government must assuredly proceed from a single source; how, then, could writing proceed from two?
Now, when achievements were complete, music was composed; when government was settled, rites were instituted. From the Three Dynasties onward, no age has ever lacked rites and music. Why, then, did Master Ouyang uniformly regard them as empty names? The sages’ rites and music do not extend beyond the activities of daily life, yet embody the Way by which different undertakings share a common reverence. They do not go beyond the institutions for ordering the world and governing its affairs, yet attain the workings by which different forms express a common love. This is what Shuhou meant by administering government through ritual. In later ages, however, what was performed at court and played at the suburban altars and ancestral temples…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者謂之禮樂其從事於政特號令兵刑之
末爾何怪乎治之不古若哉然則謂之虚
名可也漢初去古未遠似可與有為矣然
以叔孫通為之臣緜蕞野外竊先王糟粕
之餘秦儀雜就為一時苟簡之制故魯兩生
以其非興禮樂之本而却以百年後興也
蜀漢僻處一隅若無足有為矣然以諸葛
亮為之相立綱陳紀而不為近圖開誠布
公而不為小惠故程子謂其得禮樂之意
===
而許以庶幾禮樂也漢章帝永言前王明
發興作詔羣臣各盡所能至以堯作大章
一夔足矣擬之曹褒志則大矣柰何依準
舊典雜取經讖張敏已有破亂聖術之譏
而褒不足以成其志也后夔云乎哉唐文
皇夜讀周禮以為聖作詔羣臣屢為會議
至以漢章拳拳有志不就語之魏徵心則
盛矣柰何才非命世學無素業王通已有
必愧禮樂之論而徵不足以副其心也周

者謂之禮樂，其從事於政，特號令兵刑之末爾，何怪乎治之不古若哉？然則謂之虚名可也。

漢初去古未遠，似可與有為矣。然以叔孫通為之臣，緜蕞野外，竊先王糟粕之餘，秦儀雜就，為一時苟簡之制。故魯兩生以其非興禮樂之本而却，以百年後興也。蜀漢僻處一隅，若無足有為矣。然以諸葛亮為之相，立綱陳紀，而不為近圖；開誠布公，而不為小惠。故程子謂其得禮樂之意，而許以庶幾禮樂也。

漢章帝永言前王，明發興作，詔羣臣各盡所能，至以「堯作大章，一夔足矣」擬之曹褒，志則大矣。柰何依準舊典，雜取經讖，張敏已有破亂聖術之譏，而褒不足以成其志也。后夔云乎哉？唐文皇夜讀周禮，以為聖作，詔羣臣屢為會議，至以漢章拳拳有志不就語之魏徵，心則盛矣。柰何才非命世，學無素業，王通已有必愧禮樂之論，而徵不足以副其心也。周
translation_en:
…they call these things rites and music; in conducting government, they concern themselves merely with such peripheral matters as commands, military affairs, and punishments. Why wonder that their government falls short of antiquity? Thus, calling these empty names is justified.

At the beginning of the Han, antiquity was not yet far distant, and meaningful achievement seemed possible. Yet with Shusun Tong as a minister, they laid out cords and bundles of reeds in the countryside to rehearse ceremonies, appropriated the dregs left by the former kings, and mixed in Qin ceremonial practices to fashion makeshift institutions for the moment. Thus the two scholars of Lu rejected this as no foundation for establishing rites and music, holding that these could arise only after a hundred years. Shu Han occupied a remote corner, seemingly without sufficient scope for achievement. Yet with Zhuge Liang as its chief minister, it established guiding principles and set out rules without pursuing short-term designs; he acted with sincerity and impartiality rather than dispensing petty favors. Master Cheng therefore said that he grasped the meaning of rites and music, and judged him to have come close to realizing them.

Emperor Zhang of Han continually pondered the former kings and rose at dawn to undertake his work, commanding his ministers each to contribute all they could. He even compared Cao Bao to Kui, saying, “When Yao created the Great Splendor music, one Kui sufficed.” His ambition was indeed great. Yet Cao Bao relied on old precedents and drew indiscriminately upon the classics and prophetic texts; Zhang Min had already criticized him for disrupting the arts of the sages, and Bao was unequal to fulfilling the emperor’s ambition. Could he be called the Music Master Kui?

Emperor Wen of Tang read the Rites of Zhou at night, deemed it a sage’s work, and repeatedly ordered his ministers to convene for deliberations. He even spoke to Wei Zheng of Emperor Zhang of Han’s earnest but unfulfilled ambition. His aspirations were indeed lofty. Yet Wei Zheng lacked the talent of an exceptional figure born for his age and had no established foundation in learning. Wang Tong had already declared that he would surely fall short in rites and music, and Zheng was unequal to meeting the emperor’s aspirations. The Duke of Zhou…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
公云乎哉由此觀之後世禮樂不能復古
漢之雜覇唐之雜夷卒不免於公論歐陽
子所謂不可不出於一者豈欺我哉吐辭
爲經出言爲論六經之後世未嘗無文章
也何楊龜山槩謂之無益乎盖聖人之文
章形於言語闡造化精微之蘊著之簡冊
本仁義英華之發濂溪所謂文以載道是
也後世則以見於操脩措諸踐履者謂之
道德其從事於文第聲律詞藻之工爾何
===
怪乎文之不古若哉然則謂之無益可也
夫以柳子厚當百年積累之餘大放厥辭
以追往古江左之綺麗已除光嶽之精華
既聚一時文名與韓退之相爲頡頏而韓
亦稱其雄深雅健似司馬子長崔蔡不足
多也劉禹錫所謂文章與時高下不見於
此乎揚子雲慕司馬相如之才嘗擬其賦
已而棄不復爲作太玄以準易作法言以
擬論語一時君子唯桓譚以爲絕倫而譚

translation_en:
…could he be called the Duke of Zhou? Viewed in this light, the rites and music of later ages could not recover antiquity: the Han mingled the hegemonic way into its rule, and the Tang mingled in non-Chinese practices. In the end, neither escaped the judgment of the world. Could Master Ouyang have misled us when he said that these must issue from a single source? Their utterances became classics, their words became authoritative discourses. Since the Six Classics, the world has never lacked literary writings; why, then, did Yang Guishan dismiss them all as useless? The sages’ writings, expressed in language, disclose the subtle mysteries of creation; committed to bamboo slips and books, they spring from the flowering of benevolence and righteousness. This is what Lianxi meant by writing serving to convey the Way. In later ages, people called what appeared in self-cultivation and was put into practice “the Way and virtue,” while their literary pursuits consisted merely of skill in prosody and ornate diction. Why wonder that their writing did not equal that of antiquity? It is therefore permissible to call it useless.
Now Liu Zihou, coming after a hundred years of accumulated achievement, gave his expression full rein in pursuit of antiquity. The ornate style of Jiangzuo had already been swept away, and the finest essences of heaven and earth had gathered in him. His literary reputation in his day rivaled that of Han Tuizhi. Han himself praised his writing as powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous, resembling that of Sima Zichang; Cui and Cai were scarcely worth extolling by comparison. Is this not an illustration of Liu Yuxi’s statement that literature rises and falls with its age? Yang Ziyun admired Sima Xiangru’s talent and once imitated his rhapsodies. Later, he abandoned this and wrote no more of them. He composed the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan), taking the Book of Changes as his standard, and the Exemplary Sayings (Fayan), modeling it on the Analects. Among the gentlemen of his day, only Huan Tan considered him peerless; and Huan Tan…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
又稱其文義至深議論不詭于聖人遭遇
時君則必度越諸子矣龜山所謂庶幾於
道者不以是乎漢文涉八代而衰韓退之
以六經之文爲諸儒倡橫鶩別驅汪洋大
肆學者仰之以爲山斗其徒李漢稱之有
曰周情孔思卒澤於道德仁義是謂其得
周公孔子之趣也而原道之作識用遺體
朱子譏其因文見道即程子所謂作文有
得却爲倒學之意也然推尊孔子功不下
===
孟軻氏則誠有焉唐文歷五季而弊歐陽
子慕昌黎之文必欲并轡絕驅而追與之
並天下翕然尊之爲師其徒蘇軾擬之以
文王既沒文不在茲之說是謂其得文王
孔子之傳也而論性之書謂性非所先朱
子譏其未免韓病即龜山所謂性分之內
全無見處之意也然作五代史功不下司
馬遷則不誣焉由此觀之後世文章終愧
于道漢之文以貫道軾之文與道俱終未

曰周情孔思卒澤於道德仁義是謂其得
周公孔子之趣也而原道之作識用遺體
朱子譏其因文見道即程子所謂作文有
得却爲倒學之意也然推尊孔子功不下
===
孟軻氏則誠有焉唐文歷五季而弊歐陽
子慕昌黎之文必欲并轡絕驅而追與之
並天下翕然尊之爲師其徒蘇軾擬之以
文王既沒文不在兹之說是謂其得文王
孔子之傳也而論性之書謂性非所先朱
子譏其未免韓病即龜山所謂性分之内
全無見處之意也然作五代史功不下司
馬遷則不誣焉由此觀之後世文章終愧
于道漢之文以貫道軾之文與道俱終未
punctuated: 又稱其文義至深，議論不詭于聖人，遭遇時君，則必度越諸子矣。龜山所謂庶幾於道者，不以是乎？漢文涉八代而衰，韓退之以六經之文爲諸儒倡，橫鶩別驅，汪洋大肆，學者仰之以爲山斗。其徒李漢稱之有曰：「周情孔思，卒澤於道德仁義。」是謂其得周公孔子之趣也。而《原道》之作，識用遺體，朱子譏其因文見道，即程子所謂作文有得，却爲倒學之意也。然推尊孔子，功不下孟軻氏，則誠有焉。唐文歷五季而弊，歐陽子慕昌黎之文，必欲并轡絕驅而追與之並，天下翕然尊之爲師。其徒蘇軾擬之以「文王既沒，文不在茲」之說，是謂其得文王孔子之傳也。而《論性》之書，謂性非所先，朱子譏其未免韓病，即龜山所謂性分之內全無見處之意也。然作《五代史》，功不下司馬遷，則不誣焉。由此觀之，後世文章終愧于道。漢之文以貫道，軾之文與道俱，終未
translation_en:
…He further praised the profound meaning of Yang Xiong’s writings and the conformity of his arguments with the sages: had he encountered a receptive ruler of his time, he would surely have surpassed the various philosophical masters. Was this not why Guishan, Yang Shi, described him as having come close to the Way?

The prose of the Han declined over the course of eight dynasties. Han Tuizhi, Han Yu, took the writings of the Six Classics as his standard and led the scholars, ranging freely along a course of his own, expansive and unrestrained. Students looked up to him as to Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper. His follower Li Han praised him, saying: “With the feelings of the Duke of Zhou and the thoughts of Confucius, he ultimately became steeped in the Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness.” This meant that he had grasped the purport of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. Yet in his Inquiry into the Way, he recognized its function while overlooking its substance [?]. Master Zhu criticized him for apprehending the Way through literary writing. This is precisely what Master Cheng meant when he said that gaining understanding through composing prose amounted to learning in reverse order. Nevertheless, his achievement in exalting Confucius truly was no less than that of Meng Ke, Mencius.

Tang prose deteriorated through the Five Dynasties. Master Ouyang, Ouyang Xiu, admired the prose of Changli, Han Yu, and was determined to race after him at full speed, drawing abreast with reins side by side. All under Heaven unanimously revered him as a teacher. His follower Su Shi likened him to Confucius through the saying, “With King Wen now gone, does not this cultural inheritance reside here in me?” This meant that he had received the transmission of King Wen and Confucius. Yet in his writing On Human Nature, he said that human nature was not what should come first. Master Zhu criticized him for failing to escape Han Yu’s failing. This is precisely what Guishan meant by saying that he had no insight whatsoever into what lies within one’s inherent nature. Nevertheless, to say that his achievement in writing the History of the Five Dynasties was no less than Sima Qian’s is no exaggeration.

Viewed in this light, the literary writing of later ages ultimately falls short of the Way. Li Han’s notion of writing as a means of threading through the Way, and Su Shi’s notion of writing as existing together with the Way, ultimately have not yet…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
合於君子朱子所謂尤不可使出於二者
真有見哉抑嘗因是而求諸孔門其荅顔
淵之問爲邦則以四代禮樂是禮樂即所
以爲治之道也其以游夏列於文學之科
是文章不在言語之末也後世失其實而
得其名舎其本而圖其末乃曰是可以爲
治爲文矣何其不思之甚也周子曰不復
古禮不變今樂而欲至治者遠矣又曰不
務道德而第以文辭爲能者藝而已有志
===
於治與文者尚其察諸
第三問
同考試官訓導陳 批 此卷五策皆可録録
其名實一策用占其他日務實為
國家用以進配古人子尚勉之哉
同考試官訓導于 批 美名出於當時而公
論定於後世觀於吾子所評亦可謂公論矣此殆非
有窮理之學者不能非但記問之洽而已健羡健羡

於治與文者尚其察諸
第三問
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此卷五策皆可錄錄其名實一策用占其他日務實爲〕
國家用以追配古人子尚勉之哉
同考試官訓導于　批〔美名出於當時而公論定於後世觀於吾子所評亦可謂公論矣此殆非〕
有窮理之學者不能非但記問之洽而已健羨健羨
punctuated:
合於君子。朱子所謂「尤不可使出於二者」，真有見哉！抑嘗因是而求諸孔門，其荅顔淵之問爲邦，則以四代禮樂，是禮樂即所以爲治之道也。其以游夏列於文學之科，是文章不在言語之末也。後世失其實而得其名，舎其本而圖其末，乃曰：「是可以爲治爲文矣。」何其不思之甚也！周子曰：「不復古禮，不變今樂，而欲至治者，遠矣。」又曰：「不務道德，而第以文辭爲能者，藝而已。」有志於治與文者，尚其察諸！
第三問
同考試官訓導陳批：此卷五策皆可録，録其名實一策，用占其他日務實，為國家用，以進配古人。子尚勉之哉！
同考試官訓導于批：美名出於當時，而公論定於後世。觀於吾子所評，亦可謂公論矣。此殆非有窮理之學者不能，非但記問之洽而已。健羡，健羡！
translation_en:
…accord with the gentleman. Master Zhu’s remark that “one must especially not allow it to proceed from these two” [?] shows true insight! I have also pursued this matter in the teachings of Confucius. In answering Yan Yuan’s question about governing a state, he invoked the rites and music of the four dynasties: these rites and music are precisely the Way by which good government is achieved. By placing You and Xia in the category of literary learning, he showed that literary accomplishment does not belong among the lesser matters of speech. Later generations lost the substance while acquiring the name, abandoned the root while pursuing the branches, and then declared: “This will suffice for government and writing.” How utterly thoughtless!
Master Zhou said: “To seek perfect government without restoring ancient rites or changing present-day music is to remain far from the goal.” He also said: “Those who do not devote themselves to the Way and virtue, but regard skill in literary expression alone as accomplishment, possess merely an art.” May those who aspire to good government and writing examine this carefully!
Third Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: All five policy essays in this script merit inclusion. We have selected the essay on name and substance, taking it as a sign that in the future he will devote himself to substantive achievement, serve the state, and advance toward equaling the ancients. Continue to exert yourself!
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: A fine reputation arises in one’s own time, but impartial judgment is settled by later generations. Looking at your assessments, I would say that they too constitute impartial judgment. This could surely only be accomplished by someone trained in the investigation of principle; it is more than a matter of extensive memorization and acquired learning. Most admirable, most admirable!

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官左中允劉批人物一策正欲觀士子博
極之功與品題之鑒語而能詳擇而能精此作有焉本
房之冠舍子其誰
考試官侍講學士吳批古人散見簡冊一時撮取
為對頗難下筆此子能備舉之且品評甚當其亦真有
所見者乎
古之君子惟能全天下之美行而後能享
天下之美名蓋美行存乎我有不易成美
名存乎人有不易得苟行成於我而名輒
隨之固未有不可得者然或許予之過又
豈能免後世之公議哉嗟夫麟之為麟也
以德不以形驥之為驥也以德不以力夫
物且然而况美名在人有不本諸德行者
乎然非君子有心求是名也而實大聲宏
則有不可得而辭者尚何置疑於其間哉
敢因明問所及復之襄子計成智伯之讐
深矣豫讓匕首之挾蓋不能一日忘者卒
擊其衣而智伯之讐以報故曰真義士也

===

深矣豫讓匕首之挾盖不能一日忘者卒
擊其衣而智伯之讐以報故曰真義士也
punctuated:
考試官左中允劉批：人物一策，正欲觀士子博極之功與品題之鑒。語而能詳，擇而能精，此作有焉。本房之冠，舍子其誰？

考試官侍講學士吳批：古人散見簡冊，一時撮取為對，頗難下筆。此子能備舉之，且品評甚當，其亦真有所見者乎？

古之君子，惟能全天下之美行，而後能享天下之美名。蓋美行存乎我，有不易成；美名存乎人，有不易得。苟行成於我，而名輒隨之，固未有不可得者。然或許予之過，又豈能免後世之公議哉？嗟夫！麟之為麟也，以德不以形；驥之為驥也，以德不以力。夫物且然而况美名在人，有不本諸德行者乎？然非君子有心求是名也，而實大聲宏，則有不可得而辭者，尚何置疑於其間哉？敢因明問所及復之。襄子計成，智伯之讐深矣。豫讓匕首之挾，蓋不能一日忘者。卒擊其衣，而智伯之讐以報，故曰：「真義士也。」
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, Left Mentor, comments: This policy question on historical figures was intended precisely to assess the candidates’ achievement in comprehensive learning and their discernment in judging people. Detailed discussion and discerning selection are both present in this composition. Who but you could rank first in this examining room?

Examiner Wu, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: Accounts of the ancients lie scattered throughout the written records. To gather them together on the spot for an answer makes it quite difficult to begin writing. This candidate has cited them comprehensively, and his assessments are most fitting. Surely he possesses genuine insight?

Only by fully realizing the admirable conduct found under Heaven could the gentlemen of antiquity enjoy an excellent reputation throughout the world. Admirable conduct depends upon oneself and is not easily perfected; an excellent reputation depends upon others and is not easily obtained. If one perfects one’s conduct and reputation follows accordingly, such a reputation is certainly attainable. Yet if the praise bestowed is excessive, how could one escape the impartial judgment of later generations? Ah! What makes a qilin a qilin is its virtue, not its appearance; what makes a thoroughbred a thoroughbred is its quality, not its strength. If this is so even of creatures, how could a person’s excellent reputation fail to have its foundation in virtuous conduct? Yet the gentleman does not deliberately seek such a reputation. When his substantial merits are great and his renown resounding, there are honors he cannot decline. What room remains for doubt?

I venture to respond to the matters raised in your illuminating question. When Xiangzi’s scheme succeeded, the wrong suffered by Zhi Bo was grievous indeed. Yu Rang carried a dagger, unable to forget that wrong for even a single day. Finally, he struck Xiangzi’s robe, and thereby avenged Zhi Bo. Thus he was called “a truly righteous man.”

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
使襄子知而全之不爲人臣之勸乎匈奴
報至文帝之慮切矣周亞夫細柳之屯盖
方爲時所仗者竟行其令而天子之詔不
聞故曰真將軍也使文帝從而忌之是豈
任將之道乎魏相輔宣帝於中興之日而
其諫伐西域爲識兵畧作明堂月令議爲
達時令王通稱爲真漢相者非但以其能
稱上意而已賈逵當豫州凋弊之秋而外
糾貪殘以正憲度內脩政事以安吏民曹
丕稱爲真刺史者則以其能舉職任云爾
===
武德之議廢立而舉朝中立者誰不利怵
而威懼乎蕭瑀獨守正以定國儲真社稷
臣之稱太宗非以其有定守歟李密之欲
歸降而將佐貪功者誰不表獻其土地乎
李勣獨留俟密之自獻真純臣之稱太宗
非以其無所利歟書曰儆戒無虞而太平
可樂則李吉甫之面諛也李絳廷斥不避
最得大臣之體憲宗稱爲真宰相者盖見

聞故曰眞將軍也使文帝從而忌之是豈

===
丕稱爲眞刺史者則以其能舉職任云爾
武德之議廢立而舉朝中立者誰不利怵
而威懼乎蕭瑀獨守正以定國儲眞社稷
臣之稱太宗非以其有定守歟李密之欲

可樂則李吉甫之面諛也李絳廷斥不避
最得大臣之體憲宗稱爲眞宰相者盖見
punctuated:
使襄子知而全之，不爲人臣之勸乎？匈奴報至，文帝之慮切矣。周亞夫細柳之屯，盖方爲時所仗者，竟行其令，而天子之詔不聞，故曰真將軍也。使文帝從而忌之，是豈任將之道乎？魏相輔宣帝於中興之日，而其諫伐西域爲識兵畧，作明堂月令議爲達時令。王通稱爲真漢相者，非但以其能稱上意而已。賈逵當豫州凋弊之秋，而外糾貪殘以正憲度，內脩政事以安吏民。曹丕稱爲真刺史者，則以其能舉職任云爾。

武德之議廢立，而舉朝中立者，誰不利怵而威懼乎？蕭瑀獨守正以定國儲，真社稷臣之稱，太宗非以其有定守歟？李密之欲歸降，而將佐貪功者，誰不表獻其土地乎？李勣獨留俟密之自獻，真純臣之稱，太宗非以其無所利歟？《書》曰：「儆戒無虞。」而太平可樂，則李吉甫之面諛也。李絳廷斥不避，最得大臣之體。憲宗稱爲真宰相者，盖見
translation_en:
Had Xiangzi recognized his loyalty and spared him, would this not have encouraged those who serve as subjects? When reports of the Xiongnu arrived, Emperor Wen was deeply concerned. Zhou Yafu’s encampment at Xiliu was precisely what the circumstances required him to rely upon. Zhou enforced his own orders throughout, and the Son of Heaven’s command went unheeded; hence the emperor called him a true general. Had Emperor Wen thereupon become suspicious of him, could this have been the proper way to employ a general? Wei Xiang assisted Emperor Xuan during the restoration of Han rule. His remonstrance against attacking the Western Regions demonstrated his understanding of military strategy, while his composition of the Discussion of the Monthly Ordinances of the Hall of Enlightenment demonstrated his understanding of seasonal ordinances. Wang Tong’s designation of him as a true Han chief minister was not merely because he could satisfy the sovereign’s wishes. Jia Kui served when Yuzhou was impoverished and in decline. Externally, he censured the corrupt and cruel to uphold laws and standards; internally, he put administrative affairs in order to bring peace to officials and people. Cao Pi called him a true regional inspector simply because he could fulfill the responsibilities of his office.

When the question of deposing and installing the heir arose during the Wude reign, who among those throughout the court who remained neutral was not tempted by advantage and frightened by power? Xiao Yu alone upheld what was right and secured the imperial succession. Was it not because of this steadfastness that Emperor Taizong called him a true minister of the altars of soil and grain? When Li Mi wished to submit, who among the commanders and their assistants eager to claim merit did not memorialize the throne offering up his territory? Li Ji alone held back, waiting for Li Mi to offer it himself. Was it not because he sought no personal advantage that Taizong called him a truly pure minister? The Book of Documents says, “Remain vigilant and take precautions when there is no cause for anxiety.” Yet Li Jifu flattered the emperor to his face by saying that an age of peace could be enjoyed at ease. Li Jiang denounced him at court without flinching, exemplifying to the highest degree the bearing of a great minister. Emperor Xianzong called him a true chief minister, for he was recognized…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
知於其君如此語曰不辱君命而遣使雲
中則宋室之屈辱也洪皓氣不少挫卒全
使臣之節金人稱爲真忠臣者蓋見重於
外夷如此李沆相真宗嘗以四方水旱預
警其心厥後泰侈並興所言竟驗王旦嘆
其先識而稱之爲真聖人然亦晚矣唐介
劾文彥博謂以間金奇錦進由妃嬪四方
聞其直言而稱之爲真御史貶亦榮矣學
士代王言草詔其職也而宋實則當建儲
===
者王珪面受仁宗之命然後操筆歐陽脩
以真學士稱之則嘉其得慎重之意故爾
侍講備經筵進講其職也而邇英則當坐
講者程頤講說哲宗之前聳動羣聽文彥
博以真侍講稱之則重其得進講之體故
爾唐時有司鮮不市恩孰意挺立頹波中
乃有王丘崔沔裴耀卿者一則餼牽外無
他獻一則供帳無錦繡一則表獻數百言
以寓規諫玄宗總以真良吏稱之三人而

爾唐時有司鮮不市恩孰意挺立頹波中
乃有王丘崔沔裴耀卿者一則籲牽外無
他獻一則供帳無錦繡一則表獻數百言
以寓規諫玄宗總以真良吏稱之三人亦
punctuated: 知於其君如此。語曰：「不辱君命。」而遣使雲中，則宋室之屈辱也。洪皓氣不少挫，卒全使臣之節，金人稱爲真忠臣者，蓋見重於外夷如此。李沆相真宗，嘗以四方水旱預警其心；厥後泰侈並興，所言竟驗，王旦嘆其先識，而稱之爲真聖人，然亦晚矣。唐介劾文彥博，謂以間金奇錦進由妃嬪，四方聞其直言，而稱之爲真御史，貶亦榮矣。學士代王言，草詔其職也，而宋實則當建儲者，王珪面受仁宗之命，然後操筆。歐陽脩以真學士稱之，則嘉其得慎重之意故爾。侍講備經筵，進講其職也，而邇英則當坐講者，程頤講說哲宗之前，聳動羣聽。文彥博以真侍講稱之，則重其得進講之體故爾。唐時有司鮮不市恩，孰意挺立頹波中，乃有王丘、崔沔、裴耀卿者！一則餼牽外無他獻，一則供帳無錦繡，一則表獻數百言以寓規諫。玄宗總以真良吏稱之，三人而
translation_en:
…was thus appreciated by his ruler. As the saying goes, “Do not disgrace your ruler’s commission.” Yet sending an envoy to Yunzhong was a humiliation for the Song ruling house. Hong Hao’s spirit did not falter in the least, and he ultimately preserved the integrity of an envoy. The Jin people called him a truly loyal minister: such was the esteem in which he was held among foreign peoples.

When Li Hang served as chief councilor to Emperor Zhenzong, he would forewarn the emperor by reporting floods and droughts throughout the realm. Later, extravagance and luxury arose together, and his words proved true. Wang Dan marveled at his foresight and called him a true sage, but by then it was too late. Tang Jie impeached Wen Yanbo, alleging that he had secured advancement through the imperial consorts by presenting them with rare brocade interwoven with gold. People throughout the realm heard of Tang’s forthright words and called him a true censor. Even his demotion brought him honor.

An academician speaks on the sovereign’s behalf, and drafting edicts is his duty. In the Song, on an occasion when an heir apparent was to be designated [?], Wang Gui received Emperor Renzong’s command in person before taking up his brush. Ouyang Xiu called him a true academician because he commended his understanding of the need for caution and gravity. An expositor-in-waiting attends the Classics Colloquium, and delivering lectures is his duty. At the Yingying Hall, where lectures were to be delivered seated, Cheng Yi expounded the texts before Emperor Zhezong, stirring all who listened. Wen Yanbo called him a true expositor-in-waiting because he valued his grasp of the proper manner of lecturing.

In Tang times, few officials refrained from currying favor. Who would have expected Wang Qiu, Cui Mian, and Pei Yaoqing to stand firm amid this tide of decline! One offered nothing beyond provisions and livestock; another furnished the imperial lodging without embroidered fabrics or brocades; and the third presented a memorial of several hundred words conveying admonition and remonstrance. Emperor Xuanzong called them all truly good officials, and these three men…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不以為罪此蓋其初政清明乎過此則其
志荒矣蒙古諸臣鮮有全材孰意超出風
氣外乃有廉希憲者居相臣位以勳業著
聞受孔子戒以忠孝自負當時兼以宰相
中真宰相男子中真男子稱之一人而不
以為嫵此蓋其善變國俗乎下此則可稱
者少矣噫天下美名其實難副而真之為
言又皆確然之詞鸞停鵠峙播揚人口珠
聯璧合照映簡編千載之下使人聞之寧
===
不為諸君子歆豔也耶抑尤有說焉程頤
一代真儒道尊河洛李沆一時賢相名冠
元臣唐介之直同於李絳洪皓之節幾於
豫讓之數公者吾無間然乃若魏相功業
著矣而嚴切是尚有乖相體於當時王珪
文學著矣而三旨是名頗尸相位於他日
蕭瑀早失河池之節不得與堯君素而齊
名李勣贊成武氏之立乃甘與許敬宗而
同惡其顯著者且如此他可知矣然則衆

punctuated:
不以為罪，此蓋其初政清明乎？過此則其志荒矣。蒙古諸臣鮮有全材，孰意超出風氣外，乃有廉希憲者，居相臣位，以勳業著聞，受孔子戒，以忠孝自負。當時兼以宰相中真宰相、男子中真男子稱之一人，而不以為嫵，此蓋其善變國俗乎？下此則可稱者少矣。噫！天下美名，其實難副，而真之為言，又皆確然之詞。鸞停鵠峙，播揚人口；珠聯璧合，照映簡編。千載之下，使人聞之，寧不為諸君子歆豔也耶？
抑尤有說焉。程頤，一代真儒，道尊河洛；李沆，一時賢相，名冠元臣。唐介之直，同於李絳；洪皓之節，幾於豫讓。之數公者，吾無間然。乃若魏相，功業著矣，而嚴切是尚，有乖相體於當時；王珪，文學著矣，而三旨是名，頗尸相位於他日。蕭瑀早失河池之節，不得與堯君素而齊名；李勣贊成武氏之立，乃甘與許敬宗而同惡。其顯著者且如此，他可知矣。然則衆
translation_en:
…and did not regard it as an offense. Was this perhaps because his early rule was clear-sighted and enlightened? Beyond this period, his purposes became dissolute. Among the ministers of the Mongols, few possessed comprehensive talents. Who would have expected someone to rise above the prevailing customs—yet there was Lian Xixian. Occupying the position of chief councillor, he was renowned for his meritorious achievements; receiving the teachings of Confucius, he prided himself on loyalty and filial devotion. His contemporaries bestowed both descriptions upon this one man: “a true chief councillor among chief councillors” and “a true man among men,” without considering it flattering embellishment [?]. Was this perhaps because he excelled at transforming his country's customs? Below his level, few were worthy of praise. Alas! Fine reputations in this world are difficult to match in substance, and the word “true” in each of these descriptions is, moreover, an unequivocal assertion. Like luan birds alighting and swans standing tall, these praises spread from mouth to mouth; like linked pearls and paired jade discs, they illuminate the written records. A thousand years later, could anyone hearing them fail to admire and envy these gentlemen?
Yet there is more to be said. Cheng Yi was a true Confucian of his age, whose Way was revered in the He–Luo region; Li Hang was a worthy chief councillor of his time, whose reputation surpassed those of the foremost ministers. Tang Jie's uprightness equalled Li Jiang's, and Hong Hao's integrity approached Yu Rang's. With these gentlemen I can find no fault. As for Wei Xiang, however, his achievements were distinguished, but his preference for severity and strictness fell short of the bearing proper to a chief councillor in his day. Wang Gui was distinguished in literary learning, but became known for his “three responses to imperial instructions,” and in his later days largely occupied the chief councillor's post without fulfilling its duties. Xiao Yu early forfeited his integrity at Hechi and could not rank alongside Yao Junsu in reputation. Li Ji supported the enthronement of Lady Wu as empress, willingly sharing in Xu Jingzong's wrongdoing. If even the prominent figures among them were like this, the rest may readily be imagined. Then, the multitude…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
人所稱者豈皆確論哉雖然擇從其善聖
人之訓取法乎上君子之心就其中可以
為終身師範者則伊川其尤也鄙見如斯
未知能協天下公議否執事幸進教之
第四問
陳沛
同考試官學正周批天資學術皆可以建
立事功學術之偏適足以誤人家國此策於漢宋諸
人歷歷言之固見所學於末又斷以天資學術不可
===
偏廢深為有見錄之不能無補
考試官左中允劉批天資之美固當養以學術
而學術尤貴於正古人事業未有不以是為重輕者此
策歷代評之末復歸重於學有識之士也高薦允宜
考試官侍講學士吳批古人事業竒偉皆從學術
中流出間有可議者則以學術不正故耳子於是問能
以是意答之卓有定見可嘉可嘉
古人之事業有出於天資者焉有發自學
術者焉養之純者其為也有本而自無不

第四問
陳沛

同考試官學正周批：天資、學術，皆可以建立事功。學術之偏，適足以誤人家國。此策於漢、宋諸人歷歷言之，固見所學；於末又斷以天資、學術不可偏廢，深為有見，錄之不能無補。

考試官左中允劉批：天資之美，固當養以學術，而學術尤貴於正。古人事業，未有不以是為重輕者。此策歷代評之，末復歸重於學，有識之士也，高薦允宜。

考試官侍講學士吳批：古人事業竒偉，皆從學術中流出；間有可議者，則以學術不正故耳。子於是問，能以是意答之，卓有定見，可嘉，可嘉！

古人之事業，有出於天資者焉，有發自學術者焉。養之純者，其為也有本，而自無不
translation_en:
…those whom people praise—are the judgments about them all sound? Nevertheless, choosing and following what is good is the sage’s teaching; taking the highest as one’s model is the gentleman’s aspiration. Among these men, Yichuan is preeminent as a model whom one may follow throughout one’s life. Such is my humble view; I do not know whether it accords with the impartial judgment of all under Heaven. I would be grateful for your instruction.

Fourth Question
Chen Pei

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: Natural endowments and learning can both provide the basis for achievement in public affairs. One-sided learning, however, serves only to lead men astray and harm their families and states. This policy essay discusses the various figures of the Han and Song individually and clearly, demonstrating the candidate’s learning. Its concluding judgment that neither natural endowments nor learning may be neglected is deeply perceptive. Selecting it cannot fail to be beneficial.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Left Companion to the Heir Apparent: Fine natural endowments should certainly be nurtured through learning, but it is especially important that learning be correct. The worth of the achievements of men of antiquity invariably depended upon this. This policy essay assesses men of successive dynasties and concludes by again giving greatest weight to learning. Its author is a man of discernment; recommending him highly is entirely fitting.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Academician Expositor-in-Waiting: The extraordinary achievements of men of antiquity all flowed from their learning. Where there were occasionally grounds for criticism, this was simply because their learning was incorrect. In answering this question, you have expressed this principle with outstandingly firm judgment. Admirable, admirable!

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
盛禀之厚者亦往往暗合而不無可觀故
天資近道或有非學術所能先而學術有
未正焉又不若天資暗合者之為愈也君
子之於人物豈可以一律評哉請以所聞
復執事之問漢高帝之臣有周勃者焉起
于織薄而封絳侯為人重厚少文坐責諸
生趣為我語其木強可知也而帝獨以可
屬大事安劉必勃許之於是左袒一呼誅
吕立代竟成社稷之功史稱其為漢伊周
===
===
非許之哉古所謂木訥近仁者盖以此也
武帝之臣有霍光者焉階自去病而封博
陸為人不學無術洪範未聞桐宫罔識其
膚陋可知也而帝獨以可任大事圖周公
負成王賜之於是委裘有托擁昭立宣再
定廟堂之策史稱其雖伊周不過非美之
哉古所稱篤以不揜者盖以此也契丹入
寇羽書五至其勢盖岌岌矣主親征之議
畫百年之策而飲酒放歌笑謔自如卒之

盛。禀之厚者，亦往往暗合而不無可觀。故天資近道，或有非學術所能先；而學術有未正焉，又不若天資暗合者之為愈也。君子之於人物，豈可以一律評哉？請以所聞復執事之問。漢高帝之臣，有周勃者焉，起于織薄而封絳侯。為人重厚少文，坐責諸生：「趣為我語！」其木強可知也。而帝獨以「可屬大事，安劉必勃」許之。於是左袒一呼，誅吕立代，竟成社稷之功。史稱其為漢伊周，非許之哉？古所謂「木訥近仁」者，盖以此也。
武帝之臣，有霍光者焉，階自去病而封博陸。為人不學無術，《洪範》未聞，桐宫罔識，其膚陋可知也。而帝獨以可任大事，圖周公負成王賜之。於是委裘有托，擁昭立宣，再定廟堂之策。史稱其「雖伊周不過」，非美之哉？古所稱「篤以不揜」者，盖以此也。
契丹入寇，羽書五至，其勢盖岌岌矣。主親征之議，畫百年之策，而飲酒放歌，笑謔自如，卒之
translation_en:
…flourish. Those richly endowed by nature also often accord with the Way unwittingly, and their achievements are not without merit. Thus, when natural gifts approach the Way, they may possess qualities that learning cannot surpass. Conversely, where learning is not correct, it falls short of the accomplishments of those whose natural gifts accord with the Way unwittingly. How could a gentleman judge everyone by a single standard? Allow me to answer your question with what I have learned.
Among the ministers of Emperor Gao of Han was Zhou Bo, who rose from weaving mats to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang. He was grave and substantial in character but had little literary cultivation. Seated, he would demand of the scholars, “Hurry and tell me!” His bluntness and obstinacy are evident from this. Yet the emperor alone recognized him as someone to whom great affairs could be entrusted, declaring, “The man who secures the Liu house will surely be Bo.” Thereupon, with a single call to bare their left arms, he rallied his supporters, destroyed the Lü faction, and enthroned the King of Dai, ultimately rendering great service to the dynasty. The histories call him the Han dynasty’s Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou: is this not an expression of approval? This surely illustrates the ancient saying, “The unpolished and slow of speech are close to benevolence.”
Among the ministers of Emperor Wu was Huo Guang, who advanced through Huo Qubing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu. He lacked learning and scholarly accomplishment; he had not heard of the Great Plan and knew nothing of the Tong Palace. His shallow understanding is evident from this. Yet the emperor alone deemed him capable of undertaking great affairs and bestowed on him a picture of the Duke of Zhou carrying King Cheng on his back. Thus the throne left by the deceased emperor had someone to whom it could be entrusted. Huo Guang supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan, twice settling the great affairs of the court. The histories say that “even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou could not surpass him”: is this not praise? This surely illustrates what the ancients called “steadfast and without concealment” [?].
When the Khitan invaded, urgent military dispatches arrived five times, and the situation was indeed perilous. He advocated having the emperor lead the campaign in person and devised a plan for a century of security, yet drank wine, sang freely, and laughed and joked with his customary ease. In the end…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
點虜請盟弭兵南北寇萊公之績何偉也
張詠謂其不學無術比之霍光盖責備賢
者之意愚則曰天資英邁通春秋三傳豈
真光之流乎兩宮搆隙中外危懼其時盖
洶洶矣勸其母以慈勉其子以孝而垂紳
正笏不動聲色卒之光獻撤簾嗣君秉政
韓魏公之功何奇也吕中謂其重厚可任
比之周勃盖即其近似者為名愚則曰獨
觀書文晝夜不寐豈真勃之匹乎程子於
===
子房謂其有儒者氣象非以其功成引退
不邇榮利故邪然運籌帷幄之中决勝千
里之外要之不無所自學禮淮陽受書圯
上其學固有素矣程子於陳平謂其不知
道而知學非以其善言宰職為得大體故
邪然出奇裨開拓之業交歡成定策之功
要之必有所本家貧讀書治黄老術其學
亦已舊矣若漢武帝下詔求賢臨軒策問
而公孫弘起跡羊豕立談封侯正宜開陳

正笏不動聲色卒之光獻撤簾嗣君秉政
韓魏公之功何奇也呂中謂其重厚可任
比之周勃盖即其近似者爲名愚則曰獨
觀書文晝夜不寐豈真勃之匹乎程子於
===
子房謂其有儒者氣象非以其功成引退
不邇榮利故邪然運籌帷幄之中决勝千
里之外要之不無所自學禮淮陽受書圯
上其學固有素矣程子於陳平謂其不知
道而知學非以其善言宰職爲得大體故
邪然出奇裨闔拓之業交歡成定策之功
要之必有所本家貧讀書治黄老術其學
亦已舊矣若漢武帝下詔求賢臨軒策問
而公孫弘起跡羊豕立談封侯正宜開陳
punctuated: 點虜請盟，弭兵南北，寇萊公之績何偉也！張詠謂其不學無術，比之霍光，盖責備賢者之意。愚則曰：天資英邁，通《春秋》三傳，豈真光之流乎？兩宮搆隙，中外危懼，其時盖洶洶矣。勸其母以慈，勉其子以孝，而垂紳正笏，不動聲色，卒之光獻撤簾，嗣君秉政，韓魏公之功何奇也！吕中謂其重厚可任，比之周勃，盖即其近似者為名。愚則曰：獨觀書文，晝夜不寐，豈真勃之匹乎？程子於子房，謂其有儒者氣象，非以其功成引退、不邇榮利故邪？然運籌帷幄之中，决勝千里之外，要之不無所自。學禮淮陽，受書圯上，其學固有素矣。程子於陳平，謂其不知道而知學，非以其善言宰職為得大體故邪？然出奇裨開拓之業，交歡成定策之功，要之必有所本。家貧讀書，治黄老術，其學亦已舊矣。若漢武帝下詔求賢，臨軒策問，而公孫弘起跡羊豕，立談封侯，正宜開陳

Zhang Yong called him unlearned and without expertise, comparing him to Huo Guang; this surely expressed his wish to demand perfection of a worthy man. I, however, would say: endowed with exceptional talents and versed in the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, could he truly have been of Huo Guang’s sort? When a rift arose between the two palaces, fear gripped those at court and beyond, and the times were indeed turbulent. He urged the mother to show maternal kindness and encouraged the son to show filial devotion. With his ceremonial sash hanging down and his audience tablet held upright, he betrayed no agitation in voice or expression. In the end, Guangxian withdrew the curtain of her regency, and the succeeding sovereign took charge of government. How extraordinary were the accomplishments of Han, Duke of Wei! Lü Zhong described him as dignified, substantial, and worthy of great responsibility, comparing him to Zhou Bo; presumably he characterized him through their points of resemblance. I, however, would say: reading books and writings alone, remaining sleepless day and night—could he truly have been merely Zhou Bo’s equal? Master Cheng said that Zifang possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar. Was this not because, his achievements complete, he retired and kept away from honors and profit? Yet his ability to devise strategies within the command tent and determine victory a thousand li away must, after all, have had some source. He studied ritual in Huaiyang and received a book upon the bridge: his learning certainly had an established foundation. Master Cheng said of Chen Ping that, although he did not understand the Way, he understood the importance of learning. Was this not because his apt discussion of the duties of a chief councillor showed a grasp of the essentials? Yet his ingenious stratagems assisted the work of expanding the realm, and his cultivation of friendly relations enabled him to help settle the succession. These accomplishments must, after all, have had a foundation. Though his family was poor, he read books and studied the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi: his learning, too, was of long standing. He ought then to have openly expounded…

title: 正德八年順天府鄉試錄
text:
善道以承德意可也柰何誣水旱以文其
奸假儉約以售其詐徙仲舒於膠東陷主
父於刑戮而帝之好大喜功窮兵黷武曾
不能少救則其習春秋爲業以文學見徵
者豈非希世取寵之筌蹄乎趙普以潜邸
受知事無大小悉以咨决而獻可替否偃
武脩文有以定一代之規盖其少習吏事
素寡學術晚年讀書手不釋卷而遇斷大
議取决方冊所得於論語者爲獨深也不
===
然則其自稱載披典籍頗識前言者果何
物耶李沆以科甲被遇事關軍國必訪裁
處而四方水旱日以奏聞中外利害一切
報罷有以得大臣之體盖沆少而好學器
識宏遠詔書應制文理稱旨而節用愛人
使民以時體驗於論語者爲尤切也不然
則其同列稱爲聖人當時號曰聖相者果
何謂邪若宋神宗銳意太平謙諮治道而
王安石歡同魚水驟遷端揆正當日進讜
